title: Introduction
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Introduction

Dungeons & Dragons is a cooperative game in which players create exciting fantasy stories guided by a Dungeon Master, or DM. Imagination and chance determine the fate of the players' characters.

An Ongoing Game

Each time you gather to play D&D, you're playing a single game session. These sessions connect to form adventures like the ones in this product. The next time you play, the story picks up where you left off.

Choose Your Role

To play D&D with Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club, you need two to five people to play as characters and one person to be the Dungeon Master.

Playing a Character

If you want to be one of the protagonists in your group's adventures, consider playing a character. Your character is your alter ego in the fantasy world of the game. Here's what these players do.

Choose a Character

Select from the following five characters from the world of Stranger Things:

  • Lady Applejack. Played by Erica Sinclair, Lady Applejack is a Chaotic Good, Elf Rogue who will sneak behind any monster, stab them in the back with her kukri, and smile as she watches them die a slow, agonizing death.
  • Nog the Dwarf. Dustin Henderson's sturdy Cleric, Nog, has gotten his companions out of a bind more times than he can count. Nog is a devotee of Heironeous, a god of chivalry, justice, and war.
  • Sundar the Bold. A gallant and unyielding warrior, Sundar the Bold bravely defends his companions—just like this Fighter's player, Lucas Sinclair.
  • Tayr the Paladin. When Mike Wheeler isn't behind the DM screen in his parents' basement, he dusts off his trusty Paladin, Tayr. The heart of the party, Tayr unites his companions and leads the charge in their fight against evil.
  • Will the Wise. Will Byer's Wizard is a mainstay of the party and is always up for another adventure. When Will the Wise casts a spell, his magic sometimes manifests in unexpected colors.

Team Up

Your character joins the other players' characters to form an adventuring party, often referred to as "the party." These adventurers are allies who face challenges and fantastical situations together. Each character has distinctive capabilities that complement those of the other characters.

Venture Forth

Your character's group explores locations and events presented by the DM. You can respond to them however you can imagine, guided by the rules in the D&D Beyond Basic Rules. Although the DM controls all the monsters you encounter, the DM isn't your adversary. The DM guides your party's journey as your characters become more powerful.

Being the Dungeon Master

If you want to be the mastermind of the game, consider being the DM. Here's what DMs do:

  • Run the Adventure. You run one or more of the adventures.
  • Guide the Story. You narrate much of the action during play, describing locations and creatures that the adventurers face. The players decide what their characters do as they navigate hazards and choose what to explore. Then you use a combination of imagination and the game's rules to determine the results of the adventurers' decisions.
  • Adjudicate the Rules. You oversee how the group uses the game's rules, making sure the rules serve the group's fun. You'll want to read the D&D Beyond Basic Rules, and you'll find the rules glossary essential.

Don't worry, Henderson. I'm not going to leave you high and dry. Papa Bear is here. I've left notes like this throughout the adventures to give you a peek behind the scenes and help you run these adventures, but you gotta make 'em your own. You can do this. I believe in you.

Swapping Roles

Playing a character and being the Dungeon Master aren't permanent roles. Each adventure is a self-contained story. Whenever you begin an adventure, determine who will be the DM for that story.

If your group consists of five or fewer players, the previous DM can either choose from the remaining characters or play as the new DM's old character. For groups of six, the previous DM always inherits the available character. Either way, ensure that the character's level is appropriate for the upcoming adventure. The adventures span levels 1–3.

Getting Started

Once you've chosen the DM, follow the instructions below to begin play.

If You're Playing a Character

Follow these steps to prepare your character:

  • Choose a Character. Pick one of the five level 1 Characters from appendix D.
  • Review Your Character. Take a moment to look over your Character Sheet. When you're ready, introduce your character to the other players.

If You're the Dungeon Master

Follow these steps if you're the DM:

  • Review the D&D Beyond Basic Rules. Familiarize yourself with the D&D Beyond Basic Rules. You don't need to memorize every rule before you play, but you should understand the rhythm of play and where to find relevant information when needed.
  • Prepare the First Adventure. "The Vanishing Gnome" is designed for level 1 characters. Read the Key Plot Points and Adventure Background sections. These sections present important context for the adventure, though the story that ultimately emerges is the one your group experiences.

Now you're ready to play D&D. Hell yeah!

Running the Adventures

Greyhawkins

The following information is key to running the adventures.

Text that appears in a box like this is meant to be read aloud or paraphrased for the players when their characters first arrive at a location or under a specific circumstance, as described in the text.

When a monster's name appears in Bold type, that's a visual cue to say, "Hey, DM, you should get this stat block ready. You're going to need it."

Magic items are described in Appendix A, while NPCs and Monsters are described in Appendix B.

html:
The Vanishing Gnome

An Adventure for Level 1 Characters

This adventure is designed to fill one or two sessions of play.

If you aren't using the Map of Greyhawkins, it can take place in any shadowy dungeon.

Key Plot Points

This information is key to the adventure's story:

  • Plot Point 1. Flizzlebin magically contacts the characters and challenges them to find him in the Dungeon of Shadows.
  • Plot Point 2. The characters navigate the Dungeon of Shadows in search of Flizzlebin, who calls out to them from his hiding place in a twisted reflection of the dungeon connected to a mysterious realm known as the Vale of Shadows.
  • Plot Point 3. A spawn of Demogorgon, a demon lord, has escaped the Vale of Shadows. The characters first encounter the creature in the Dungeon of Shadows, but it likely escapes.
  • Plot Point 4. After defeating the Demogorgon Spawn, the characters find Flizzlebin and earn the gnome's reward.

DM Preparation

Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

  • Step 1. Read the "Adventure Background" section.
  • Step 2. Read the "Hide-and-Seek" section and secretly note Flizzlebin's hiding spot.

Don't let anyone from Hawkins PD catch you with this. Officer Callahan still thinks I stole all those lawn gnomes that went missing a few years back. Consider this booklet evidence.

  • Step 3. Familiarize yourself with the creatures in this adventure, which are as follows:
  • 1 Demogorgon Spawn
  • Flizzlebin
  • 1 Giant Spider
  • 3 Gnoll Warrior
  • 2 Myconid Adult
  • 3 Goblin Warrior
  • 1 Shadow
  • 4 Shrieker Fungus
  • Step 4. Familiarize yourself with the magic items in this adventure, which are as follows:
  • Cap of Vanishing
  • +1 Flail
  • Flame Tongue Greatsword
  • 2 Potion of Healing
  • Wand of Secrets

Player Assistance

You can simplify the DM's role by having the a player handle tasks typically assigned to the DM. Before play begins, see if a player would like to be the Rules Consultant. That player references the D&D Beyond Basic Rules as needed.

Adventure Background

Flizzlebin, the Vanishing Gnome, tests the mettle of would-be heroes in dangerous games of hide-and-seek in dungeons throughout the land. Over the years, the elusive gnome has magically contacted countless travelers, but few have accepted his quests—and fewer have completed them. Successful seekers have emerged from these dungeons with priceless treasures and pockets brimming with gold.

Recently, Flizzlebin vanished to the Dungeon of Shadows, a maze that borders a gloomy, monster-infested realm. There, his calls to adventurers awakened a foul creature: a spawn of the demon lord Demogorgon! As Flizzlebin eagerly broadcasts his quest, the ravenous demon stalks the dungeon, complicating the gnome's game and endangering all who seek him.

Hide-and-Seek

Flizzlebin hides in the Shadow Dungeon, a mirror of the Dungeon of Shadows. Roll on the Flizzlebin's Hiding Spot table to determine where the characters can find the gnome in the dungeon (detailed later in this adventure). Flizzlebin avoids harm in his hiding place by using his Cap of Vanishing.

Flizzlebin's Hiding Spot
1d6Location
1Chamber of Bad Choices (area S1)
2Wasteland of Filthy Vines (area S2)
3Labyrinth of Gloom (area S3)
4Forge of Annihilation (area S4)
5Den of Bitsy (area S5)
6Altar of Vecna (area S6)

Beginning the Adventure

When the players are ready to begin the adventure, read or paraphrase the following text:

You travel a well-trod road through craggy and forested country. As you pass a dense thicket, a voice calls out to you exuberantly.

"Well-met, adventurers! 'Tis I, Flizzlebin, the Vanishing Gnome, the illustrious vagabond, the emissary of evasion! I have sequestered myself deep within the fabled Dungeon of Shadows, where I wait with a magical reward for those who prove themselves worthy. Find me, and the treasure is yours. Travel east to find the dungeon's entrance. Beware! Horrid creatures lurk within the dungeon's darkest corners... and so do I."

The voice fades. Do you accept this quest?

At your discretion, one or more of the characters might have heard of Flizzlebin from stories shared in taverns throughout the land. If the characters follow the gnome's instructions, they quickly arrive at the Dungeon of Shadows.

I've run this adventure a bunch of times. Every once in a while, I wind up with a player who has played the damn thing already, and you will, too. My advice? Never run it the same way twice. Hide Flizzlebin somewhere else. Add a couple of Vine Blights to the Shadow Dungeon. That'll keep everyone on their toes and stop blabbermouths from spoiling the fun for the newbies—and themselves.

A howling stone tunnel marks the entrance to the Dungeon of Shadows

Dungeon of Shadows

The Dungeon of Shadows is the bridge between Greyhawkins and the Vale of Shadows, a mirror world in a realm of shadow. Bloodthirsty gnolls, giant arachnids, deadly traps, and worse terrors await visitors to the dungeon.

A warped version of the dungeon is reflected within the Vale of Shadows. Flizzlebin hides within this shadow of the dungeon above, which is accessible only through portals hidden throughout the dungeon.

Arriving at the Dungeon

When the characters arrive at the Dungeon of Shadows, read or paraphrase the following text:

You reach the entrance to the Dungeon of Shadows. Black briars grow around the entrance's mouth, which resembles a howling stone face. Past the opening, rough-hewn stairs descend into darkness.

A character can inspect the entrance and make one of the following checks to recall lore about the dungeon and the gloomy realm it borders:

12 Intelligence (History). Monsters infest this dungeon, which is suffused with shadowy magic. The dungeon was once a temple devoted to a long-forgotten god, and its reputation is as tenebrous as its entrance. Rumors speak of a second, more sinister dungeon connected to this one.

12 Intelligence (Arcana). The dungeon is magically linked to the Vale of Shadows, a grim reflection of the natural world. Dreadful creatures and living shadows lurk in this dark and twisted reality; occasionally, some of these creatures escape the vale to plague the people of Greyhawkins.

The staircase descends 60 feet to area D1. When the characters enter the dungeon, use the Dungeon of Shadows Map to see where the characters begin in that area.

Flizzlebin can speak to the characters whenever you want him to. If your players are really green, he can be the voice of the DM, A.K.A. the voice of reason. He might contact the characters to drop a hint, give words of encouragement... or warn them of CERTAIN DEATH.

  • DM Secret!. The map for this adventure depicts the Dungeon of Shadows and its reflection in the Vale of Shadows. Keep the Vale of Shadows hidden from your players until they enter it, as detailed later in this adventure.

Dungeon Features

The dungeon has the following features:

  • Ceilings. The ceilings are 20 feet high in rooms and 10 feet high in passages.
  • Doors and Secret Doors. Doors are unlocked and made of basalt. Secret doors manifest as spidery, elastic fissures that blend in with their surroundings. As a Search action, a character can examine a wall that contains a secret door and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, noticing it on a successful check. A secret door opens as easily as any normal door.
  • Lighting. Torches in iron wall sconces fill the dungeon with Bright Light.

Dungeon Locations

The following locations are keyed to the Dungeon of Shadows map. The map also indicates where each character begins in the dungeon.

D1: Chamber of Choice

This chamber has five stone doors, each bearing a different image and inscription.

The torches in the chamber flicker as a faint, disembodied voice calls to you. "I'm pleased you have accepted my quest," says Flizzlebin. "I am here, but I am not here. Find me, and I shall reward you greatly. Be forewarned! You are not the only creatures who seek me in this accursed place." A monstrous roar echoes throughout the dungeon.

Flizzlebin speaks to the characters from the Shadow Dungeon (detailed later in this adventure). The gnome magically contacts the characters as they explore the dungeon, but he doesn't say anything else to characters in this area unless you decide otherwise. Flizzlebin has discovered that his communications have attracted the spawn of Demogorgon (see area D3), and he doesn't want to further draw its ire.

Doors

Each of the five doors is adorned with a relief sculpture and an inscription as follows:

  • Door to D2 This door bears the image of a fuming urn. The inscription reads "Wasteland of Filth."
  • Door to D3 This door bears a relief of a ferocious, many-horned minotaur above a stone maze. The inscription reads "Labyrinth of Doom."
  • Door to D4 In this door's relief, three mischievous creatures with pointed ears and sharp teeth surround an anvil. The inscription reads, "Forge of Gibbletrax."
  • Door to D5 A spiderweb is etched into this door. The inscription reads "Den of Itsy."
  • Door to D6 Etched into this door is the image of a scowling, bipedal hyenoid warrior. The door's inscription reads "Altar of Yeenoghu."

D2: Wasteland of Filth

A putrid stench hangs in this room. Gnawed bones, rotten food, and ancient junk litter the stone floor.

This room holds refuse discarded by the dungeon's denizens.

Treasure

As a Search action, a character can sift through the trash and make a 12 Wisdom (Perception) check. The first character to succeed on the check unearths five ivory urns. Each urn is worth 10 GP. Four of the urns are empty, but one contains a Potion of Healing and a tiny pewter statue of a two-headed demon worth 90 GP. A character who inspects the statue and succeeds on a 13 Intelligence (Religion) check recognizes the statue as an idol of the demon lord Demogorgon.

D3: Labyrinth of Doom

The torches along the walls of this maze begin to flicker, and a familiar disembodied voice says, "Many adventurers have met their demise in these corridors. Beware the fearsome minotaur!"

A spawn of Demogorgon feeds on its latest victim

Until recently, a bloodthirsty minotaur ruled this trap-filled labyrinth. However, an even more vicious creature—the spawn of Demogorgon, a demon lord—escaped the Vale of Shadows and slew the minotaur. The spawn is devouring the minotaur's corpse in the middle of the labyrinth.

Spear Traps

The labyrinth contains three spear traps triggered by pressure plates hidden in the floor, as denoted with a "T" on the Dungeon of Shadows map. Cobwebs and dust obscure the holes that house these spears.

Each spear trap has the following rules:

  • Detect and Disarm. As a Search action, a character can examine the walls and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, detecting the holes on a successful check. Alternatively, a character can take the Study action to inspect the floor and make a 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, detecting the pressure plate on a successful check.
  • Triggering the Trap. When a creature moves onto a trap's pressure plate for the first time on a turn, spears thrust out from the walls. Each creature on the pressure plate must succeed on a 13 Dexterity Saving Throw or be struck by a spear, taking 1d6 Piercing damage. The spears then retract, and the trap resets immediately.

Terror in the Maze

When the characters reach the center of the maze, read or paraphrase the following text:

The torches in this bloodstained corridor sputter erratically. A thin, sinewy creature with slimy, gray skin and elongated limbs crouches over a slain minotaur. The corpse squelches and snaps unsettlingly as the creature gorges on it. A small chest lies beside the mangled minotaur.

The Demogorgon Spawn continues devouring the minotaur for 1 minute or until it detects the characters. The spawn is Hostile [Attitude] toward all other creatures.

This encounter is pretty tough. Go easy on them... unless they're being ********, in which case you should give 'em hell.

To sneak past the spawn while it feeds, a character must succeed on a 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check. On a failed check, or if the characters otherwise disturb the spawn, it turns toward the adventurers. When that happens, read or paraphrase the following text:

The creature turns toward you, and its faceless head peels back to reveal five toothed, fleshy petals around a gaping mouth. It screeches and rushes toward you.

Roll Initiative!

The Demogorgon spawn fights until it is reduced to 25 Hit Points or fewer, at which point it retreats through the secret door to area S3 of the Shadow Dungeon (detailed later in this adventure). If the characters manage to defeat the Demogorgon spawn here, the adventure doesn't end; the characters still must find Flizzlebin to complete his quest.

If the characters don't disturb the spawn and aren't detected, the creature finishes its meal and then relocates to area S4 in the Shadow Dungeon.

Secret Door

A secret door (see "Dungeon Features") is set into the wall in the southeast corner of the labyrinth. It leads to area S3. Characters who witnessed the Demogorgon spawn use this secret door automatically succeed on checks to find the door.

Treasure

The chest in the middle of the labyrinth contains a Wand of Secrets and 25 GP.

D4: Forge of Gibbletrax

Clanging hammers ring out in this sweltering chamber. Three goblin smiths cluster around a glowing forge in the center of the room. The goblins sing in scratchy tones as they work:

"Deep within the Dungeon of Shadows,

We strengthen steel to slay the beasts.

Upside down in the Vale of Shadows,

Brave heroes delve to keep us free."

Blessed by a long-forgotten god, the Forge of Gibbletrax is a magic forge stewarded by three Goblin Warrior named Ble, Gib, and Trax. These smiths craft gear to defend against the dungeon's threats.

The goblins are initially Friendly [Attitude] toward the characters but defend themselves if necessary. If the characters approach the goblins peacefully, the goblins greet the characters warmly and ask what brings them to the dungeon.

Ble, Glib, and Trax usually keep to themselves, but they recently clashed with the gnolls in area D6, whose profane rituals threaten the sanctity of the forge. If the characters agree to end the gnolls' foul rites, the goblins vow to imbue the characters' weapons with the forge's magic.

Forge of Gibbletrax

The goblins' magical forge can temporarily infuse weapons and ammunition with immense heat. As a Bonus Action, a character can dip one weapon or piece of ammunition into the forge, coating it in a thin layer of molten ore. A creature that takes damage from the ore-coated weapon or ammunition takes an extra 1d6 Fire damage. Once coated, the weapon retains its heat for 10 minutes or until its damage is dealt, whichever comes first.

A character can benefit from the Forge of Gibbletrax only once, unless the goblins permit them to do so again. If all three goblins are slain or the forge is removed from this area, its magic ceases to function.

Three goblin smiths—Ble, Gib, and Trax—gleefully toil away at their magic forge while singing a work song

You can do this!

Sure, these smiths could have been dwarves, but that would've been BORING. Anyone can be a smith, just like anyone can be a Dungeon Master.

D5: Den of Itsy

Thick, sticky webs cover this once-regal chamber. Skeletons encased in cocoons hang from webs on the ceiling as grim warnings to all who enter.

A cobwebbed statue of an eight-foot-tall, armor-clad knight presides over the chamber. Before it is a stone pedestal, atop which rests a shimmering crystal spider roughly five feet in diameter. A fiery greatsword burns within the crystal spider's body, casting a warm, orange glow on the tangled nest.

  • DM Secret!. Don't reveal the Giant Spider yet. This monster is hiding.

This room is the nest of Itsy, a Giant Spider that preys on any who enter its lair. The Hostile [Attitude] spider clings to the ceiling, guarding the secret door and treasure in this room (detailed below). If a character opens the secret door or disturbs the crystal spider, Itsy begins combat.

Crystal Spider

The crystal spider is a Medium object with AC 13, HP 50, Resistance to Piercing and Slashing damage, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Destroying the crystal spider frees the treasure inside (detailed below).

Secret Door

Set into the east wall of this room is a secret door (see "Dungeon Features") that connects to area S5.

Statue

The statue depicts a knight in a gallant pose. As a Study action, a character can examine the statue and make a 12 Intelligence (Investigation) check. On a successful check, the character realizes the statue's base is unstable; a significant push could topple the statue.

As an action, a character within 5 feet of the statue can make a 10 Strength (Athletics) check to topple the statue into a space within 5 feet of it, doing so on a successful check. When the statue topples, each creature beneath it takes 4d6 Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition. The statue crumbles on impact, revealing a treasure hidden inside it (see "Treasure" below).

Webs

The web-filled areas are Difficult Terrain.

A creature that enters a web-filled area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a 12 Dexterity Saving Throw or have the Restrained condition. As an action, a creature Restrained by the webs can try to escape from them, doing so with a successful 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

Each 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect] of webs has AC 10; HP 7; Vulnerability to Fire damage; and Immunity to Piercing, Poison, and Psychic damage.

Treasure

Inside the statue is a heart-shaped emerald worth 30 GP. The sword encased in the crystal spider is a Flame Tongue Greatsword.

D6: Altar of Yeenoghu

In this square chamber, three hyenoid warriors kneel before an altar bearing a wicked-looking flail. Two of the creatures cackle maniacally as the third—the mangiest of the three who's nearly devoid of hair—chants, "Yeenoghu! Hear our laughter and let there be bloodshed and butchery!" The flail glows with sickly light.

These three Gnoll Warrior worship Yeenoghu, a merciless demon lord who delights in slaughter. The Hostile [Attitude] gnolls fight all other creatures on sight.

Completing the Ritual

If the characters don't interrupt the gnolls, they continue their ritual. After 1 minute, booming laughter erupts from the altar. Any creatures other than the gnolls in this area must make a 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 1d8 Thunder damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

After the ritual, the gnolls leave to battle the goblins in area D4. If the characters don't intervene, the gnolls overpower the goblins, and the Forge of Gibbletrax loses its magic forever.

Treasure

The flail on the altar is a +1 Flail.

Shadow Dungeon

Beneath the Dungeon of Shadows lies the Shadow Dungeon, a gloomy reflection of the dungeon that borders the Vale of Shadows. Though its chambers mirror the areas above, their contents differ, distorted by the eerie realm they border.

Finding Flizzlebin

To find Flizzlebin, the characters must defeat the Demogorgon spawn and any Hostile [Attitude] creatures in Flizzlebin's hiding spot (see the "Hide-and-Seek" section earlier in this adventure). When both conditions are met, the gnome appears to the characters; proceed to this adventure's conclusion.

If the characters reach Flizzlebin's hiding spot before they vanquish the Demogorgon spawn, read or paraphrase the following text:

"Ah! You found my hiding spot! But your work isn't done yet," says a familiar voice. "To claim your prize, you must slay the horrid creature that hunts me."

Flizzlebin doesn't bequeath his reward until the characters comply with his instructions. At your discretion, he might reveal the Demogorgon spawn's location—likely area S4.

Shadow Dungeon Features

The Shadow Dungeon has the following features:

  • Ceilings. The ceilings are 20 feet high in rooms and 10 feet high in passages.
  • Lighting. The dungeon is unlit. Area descriptions assume the characters have a light source or other means of seeing in Darkness. Bare iron sconces line the walls.
  • Doors and Secret Doors. Doors are unlocked and made of basalt. Secret doors manifest as spidery, elastic fissures that blend in with their surroundings and exude faint rays of natural light when opened. As a Search action, a character can examine a wall that contains a secret door and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, noticing it on a successful check.

Shadow Dungeon Locations

The characters can enter and leave the Shadow Dungeon through the secret door that connects areas D3 and S3 or the secret door that connects areas D5 and S5. The following locations are keyed to the upside-down portion of the Dungeon of Shadows map.

S1: Chamber of Bad Choices

This eerie chamber has five stone doors, each bearing a vile image and inscription. A dead dwarf is slumped in a shadowy corner. The corpse clutches a torn sheet of parchment in its stiff hand. Near the dwarf, a stone staircase blocked by rubble ascends into darkness.

This room mirrors the Chamber of Choice (area D1). The corpse is that of a dwarf explorer who perished four days ago while searching for Flizzlebin. The dwarf was killed by an Undead shadow.

The dwarf's body is unnaturally thin, and its clothes look too big. A character can inspect the corpse and make a 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check. On a successful check, the character discerns the dwarf's life was sapped by a supernatural force.

The dwarf clutches a note. If the characters remove it from the corpse, show the players the Dungeon Warning Handout. After the characters read the note, a Shadow rises from the dwarf's corpse and begins combat.

Dungeon Warning Handout

Doors

Each of the five doors is adorned with a relief sculpture and an inscription as follows:

  • Door to S2 (Urn). This door bears the image of an urn wrapped in ink-black vines. The inscription reads "Wasteland of Filthy Vines."
  • Door to S3 (Labyrinth). This door's relief depicts a fungal maze. The inscription reads, "Labyrinth of Gloom."
  • Door to S4 (Spiked Anvil). In this door's relief, a shadowy figure looms over a spiked anvil. The inscription reads, "Forge of Annihilation."
  • Door to S5 (Web). A black spiderweb is etched into this door. The inscription reads "Den of Bitsy."
  • Door to S6 (Hand and Eye). A desiccated hand holding an eye decorates this door. Deep scratches make the inscription illegible.

Staircase

The staircase, blocked by rubble, leads to the Vale of Shadows. That realm and its contents are beyond the scope of this adventure, but you can flesh them out as you see fit. Otherwise, the staircase is impassible.

S2: Wasteland of Filthy Vines

Slithering black vines squirm along the floor of this trash-filled room.

This room mirrors the Wasteland of Filth (area D2). The floor is Difficult Terrain.

Treasure

The first character to sift through the trash and succeed on a 12 Wisdom (Perception) check unearths five cracked urns hewn from black granite. The urns are worthless. Four of the urns are empty, but one contains a Potion of Healing and a glass eye with an emerald pupil worth 10 GP.

S3: Labyrinth of Gloom

Clouds of spores drift throughout this stone labyrinth. The maze is overgrown with fungi and foot-tall mushrooms that sprout from the walls and floor.

This stone maze mirrors the Labyrinth of Doom (area D3). The maze is home to toxic plants and four Shrieker Fungus. Two Hostile [Attitude] Myconid Adult also roam the maze, fighting any non-Plants they encounter.

If the shriekers sound off, the myconids investigate the disturbance. The shriekers don't shriek if the myconids come within 30 feet of them.

Secret Door

A secret door (see "Shadow Dungeon Features") is set into the wall near the southeast corner of the maze. It leads to area D3.

Spore Traps

The labyrinth contains three spore traps—swollen plant bulbs that exhale puffs of toxic spores—triggered by stepping on pressure plates of inflated mushrooms. These traps are marked on Dungeon of Shadows map with a "T." The fungus-infested walls obscure the bulbs that spray these spores.

Each spore trap has the following rules:

  • Detect and Disarm. As a Study action, a character can examine the walls and make a 15 Intelligence (Nature) check, identifying the toxic bulbs on a successful check. Alternatively, a character can take the Study action to inspect the floor and make a 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, identifying the fungal pressure plate on a successful check. Trimming the stems that connect the bulbs to the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.
  • Triggering the Trap. When a creature moves onto a pressure plate for the first time on a turn, the bulbs spray toxic spores that fill a 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect] centered on the pressure plate. Each creature in the Cube must succeed on a 13 Constitution Saving Throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. The trap resets immediately.

Treasure

A dilapidated chest in the middle of the labyrinth contains a broken wand and 25 GP. The wand is useless.

S4: Forge of Annihilation

An unholy forge dominates this grim chamber. Caustic fumes waft from its icy hearth, which swirls with a faintly glowing, pale-green slurry. Skulls bob along the liquid's surface.

This room mirrors the Forge of Gibbletrax (area D4). If the Demogorgon spawn survived its previous encounter with the characters (see area D3), it lurks here. Read or paraphrase the following text:

A familiar, horrible creature—the same creature you encountered in the labyrinth above—rises from the shadow of the forge. It unfurls its faceless head once more and chitters in anticipation.

Roll Initiative!

The Demogorgon Spawn fights to the death.

Forge of Annihilation

Unlike the goblins' blessed forge in the dungeon above, this forge is a cursed apparatus capable only of destruction. The Forge of Annihilation causes living creatures to wither and die. As a Study action, a character can inspect the forge and make a 13 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a successful check, the character identifies the eldritch hazard and the threat it poses.

A creature that enters the forge for the first time or starts its turn there must make a 15 Constitution Saving Throw, taking 4d8 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The Forge of Annihilation—a sinister reflection of the Forge of Gibbletrax—looms within the Shadow Dungeon

S5: Den of Bitsy

A statue of an eight-foot-tall knight with a horned, crimson helm stands in this chamber, which is covered in thick, black webs. Atop an altar in the center of the room, a massive spider with dripping fangs wraps a dead elf in webs.

Humanoid-shaped cocoons—the arachnid's ghastly larder—hang throughout the chamber.

This room mirrors the Den of Itsy (area D5). It belongs to Bitsy, an equally territorial Giant Spider. Bitsy fights the characters on sight.

Secret Door

Set into the east wall in this room is a secret door (see "Shadow Dungeon Features") that connects to area D5.

Statue

The statue depicts a knight with a menacing helm. As a Study action, a character can examine the statue and make a 12 Intelligence (Investigation) check. On a successful check, the character realizes the statue's base is unstable; a significant push could topple the statue.

As an action, a character within 5 feet of the statue can make a 10 Strength (Athletics) check to topple the statue into a space within 5 feet of it, doing so on a successful check. When the statue topples, each creature beneath it takes 4d6 Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition. The statue crumbles on impact, revealing treasure within (see "Treasure" below), but its helm remains intact.

Webs

The web-filled areas are Difficult Terrain.

A creature that enters a web-filled area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a 12 Dexterity Saving Throw or have the Restrained condition. As an action, a creature Restrained by the webs can try to escape from them, doing so with a successful 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

Each 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect] of webs has AC 10; HP 7; Vulnerability to Fire damage; and Immunity to Piercing, Poison, and Psychic damage.

Treasure

The statue's helmet is a crimson Dread Helm that resembles the head of a horned devil. Inside the statue is a heart-shaped black tourmaline worth 30 GP.

S6: Altar of Vecna

Low fog pervades this eerily quiet chamber. A stone altar rises from the center of the floor. Atop the altar, a dismembered hand grasps an hourglass half-filled with black sand and adorned with bone spindles. The sand defies gravity, flowing to the top bulb.

This room mirrors the Altar of Yeenoghu (area D6), but this altar honors evil of a viler caliber.

The first character to inspect the hourglass hears the sound of a ticking clock, followed by a baleful chime. The hourglass then cracks, and the sand spills out, revealing a mummified eye within the lower bulb. No other character hears the sound.

Afterward, a character can examine the altar's contents and make a 12 Intelligence (Religion) check. On a successful check, the character recognizes the hand and the eye as the symbol of Vecna, a powerful lich feared throughout Greyhawkins. The hourglass is a ceremonial object used by members of Vecna's cult to symbolize the lich's dreaded—and inevitable—return.

Conclusion

After the characters defeat the Demogorgon spawn and locate Flizzlebin, the gnome rewards them. Read or paraphrase the following:

A bearded gnome in a fancy cap addresses you enthusiastically. "Bravery, majesty, and teamwork!" he exclaims. "How wonderful it was to guide you on your quest." He removes his cap.

"For your heroism, I bestow on you my magic cap. But know this: The real treasures were the bonds you formed along the way.

"Go forth! Many great adventures await you."

For their efforts, Flizzlebin gives the characters his Cap of Vanishing. If one of the characters didn't find a magic item during the adventure, the gnome presents the cap to that character.

Flizzlebin is Friendly [Attitude] and willing to speak to the characters. During conversation, he fondly recalls the characters' deeds and commends them on their creativity, heroism, or any other qualities you deem appropriate. He then wishes them farewell and vanishes once more, disappearing to a faraway dungeon to challenge a new group of adventurers.

Character Advancement

After the characters receive Flizzlebin's reward, everyone in the party gains 1 level. Direct each player to record any treasure they found over the course of this adventure.

You can bring back Flizzlebin the next time you want to send the characters to a dungeon or reward a player with an item they've been pestering you about. Mike is the worst with this.

"Eddie! When are we going to level up?"

"Eddie! When do I get a Vorpal Sword?"

Obnoxious. Make him work for it.

DM Preparation

Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

  • Step 1. Read the "Adventure Background" section.
  • Step 2. Read the "Hide-and-Seek" section and secretly note Flizzlebin's hiding spot.

Don't let anyone from Hawkins PD catch you with this. Officer Callahan still thinks I stole all those lawn gnomes that went missing a few years back. Consider this booklet evidence.

  • Step 3. Familiarize yourself with the creatures in this adventure, which are as follows:
  • 1 Demogorgon Spawn
  • Flizzlebin
  • 1 Giant Spider
  • 3 Gnoll Warrior
  • 2 Myconid Adult
  • 3 Goblin Warrior
  • 1 Shadow
  • 4 Shrieker Fungus
  • Step 4. Familiarize yourself with the magic items in this adventure, which are as follows:
  • Cap of Vanishing
  • +1 Flail
  • Flame Tongue Greatsword
  • 2 Potion of Healing
  • Wand of Secrets

Player Assistance

You can simplify the DM's role by having the a player handle tasks typically assigned to the DM. Before play begins, see if a player would like to be the Rules Consultant. That player references the D&D Beyond Basic Rules as needed.

html:
Adventure Background

Flizzlebin, the Vanishing Gnome, tests the mettle of would-be heroes in dangerous games of hide-and-seek in dungeons throughout the land. Over the years, the elusive gnome has magically contacted countless travelers, but few have accepted his quests—and fewer have completed them. Successful seekers have emerged from these dungeons with priceless treasures and pockets brimming with gold.

Recently, Flizzlebin vanished to the Dungeon of Shadows, a maze that borders a gloomy, monster-infested realm. There, his calls to adventurers awakened a foul creature: a spawn of the demon lord Demogorgon! As Flizzlebin eagerly broadcasts his quest, the ravenous demon stalks the dungeon, complicating the gnome's game and endangering all who seek him.

Hide-and-Seek

Flizzlebin hides in the Shadow Dungeon, a mirror of the Dungeon of Shadows. Roll on the Flizzlebin's Hiding Spot table to determine where the characters can find the gnome in the dungeon (detailed later in this adventure). Flizzlebin avoids harm in his hiding place by using his Cap of Vanishing.

Flizzlebin's Hiding Spot
1d6Location
1Chamber of Bad Choices (area S1)
2Wasteland of Filthy Vines (area S2)
3Labyrinth of Gloom (area S3)
4Forge of Annihilation (area S4)
5Den of Bitsy (area S5)
6Altar of Vecna (area S6)

Beginning the Adventure

When the players are ready to begin the adventure, read or paraphrase the following text:

You travel a well-trod road through craggy and forested country. As you pass a dense thicket, a voice calls out to you exuberantly.

"Well-met, adventurers! 'Tis I, Flizzlebin, the Vanishing Gnome, the illustrious vagabond, the emissary of evasion! I have sequestered myself deep within the fabled Dungeon of Shadows, where I wait with a magical reward for those who prove themselves worthy. Find me, and the treasure is yours. Travel east to find the dungeon's entrance. Beware! Horrid creatures lurk within the dungeon's darkest corners... and so do I."

The voice fades. Do you accept this quest?

At your discretion, one or more of the characters might have heard of Flizzlebin from stories shared in taverns throughout the land. If the characters follow the gnome's instructions, they quickly arrive at the Dungeon of Shadows.

I've run this adventure a bunch of times. Every once in a while, I wind up with a player who has played the damn thing already, and you will, too. My advice? Never run it the same way twice. Hide Flizzlebin somewhere else. Add a couple of Vine Blights to the Shadow Dungeon. That'll keep everyone on their toes and stop blabbermouths from spoiling the fun for the newbies—and themselves.

A howling stone tunnel marks the entrance to the Dungeon of Shadows

title: Dungeon of Shadows
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Dungeon of Shadows

The Dungeon of Shadows is the bridge between Greyhawkins and the Vale of Shadows, a mirror world in a realm of shadow. Bloodthirsty gnolls, giant arachnids, deadly traps, and worse terrors await visitors to the dungeon.

A warped version of the dungeon is reflected within the Vale of Shadows. Flizzlebin hides within this shadow of the dungeon above, which is accessible only through portals hidden throughout the dungeon.

Arriving at the Dungeon

When the characters arrive at the Dungeon of Shadows, read or paraphrase the following text:

You reach the entrance to the Dungeon of Shadows. Black briars grow around the entrance's mouth, which resembles a howling stone face. Past the opening, rough-hewn stairs descend into darkness.

A character can inspect the entrance and make one of the following checks to recall lore about the dungeon and the gloomy realm it borders:

12 Intelligence (History). Monsters infest this dungeon, which is suffused with shadowy magic. The dungeon was once a temple devoted to a long-forgotten god, and its reputation is as tenebrous as its entrance. Rumors speak of a second, more sinister dungeon connected to this one.

12 Intelligence (Arcana). The dungeon is magically linked to the Vale of Shadows, a grim reflection of the natural world. Dreadful creatures and living shadows lurk in this dark and twisted reality; occasionally, some of these creatures escape the vale to plague the people of Greyhawkins.

The staircase descends 60 feet to area D1. When the characters enter the dungeon, use the Dungeon of Shadows Map to see where the characters begin in that area.

Flizzlebin can speak to the characters whenever you want him to. If your players are really green, he can be the voice of the DM, A.K.A. the voice of reason. He might contact the characters to drop a hint, give words of encouragement... or warn them of CERTAIN DEATH.

  • DM Secret!. The map for this adventure depicts the Dungeon of Shadows and its reflection in the Vale of Shadows. Keep the Vale of Shadows hidden from your players until they enter it, as detailed later in this adventure.

Dungeon Features

The dungeon has the following features:

  • Ceilings. The ceilings are 20 feet high in rooms and 10 feet high in passages.
  • Doors and Secret Doors. Doors are unlocked and made of basalt. Secret doors manifest as spidery, elastic fissures that blend in with their surroundings. As a Search action, a character can examine a wall that contains a secret door and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, noticing it on a successful check. A secret door opens as easily as any normal door.
  • Lighting. Torches in iron wall sconces fill the dungeon with Bright Light.

Dungeon Locations

The following locations are keyed to the Dungeon of Shadows map. The map also indicates where each character begins in the dungeon.

D1: Chamber of Choice

This chamber has five stone doors, each bearing a different image and inscription.

The torches in the chamber flicker as a faint, disembodied voice calls to you. "I'm pleased you have accepted my quest," says Flizzlebin. "I am here, but I am not here. Find me, and I shall reward you greatly. Be forewarned! You are not the only creatures who seek me in this accursed place." A monstrous roar echoes throughout the dungeon.

Flizzlebin speaks to the characters from the Shadow Dungeon (detailed later in this adventure). The gnome magically contacts the characters as they explore the dungeon, but he doesn't say anything else to characters in this area unless you decide otherwise. Flizzlebin has discovered that his communications have attracted the spawn of Demogorgon (see area D3), and he doesn't want to further draw its ire.

Doors

Each of the five doors is adorned with a relief sculpture and an inscription as follows:

  • Door to D2 This door bears the image of a fuming urn. The inscription reads "Wasteland of Filth."
  • Door to D3 This door bears a relief of a ferocious, many-horned minotaur above a stone maze. The inscription reads "Labyrinth of Doom."
  • Door to D4 In this door's relief, three mischievous creatures with pointed ears and sharp teeth surround an anvil. The inscription reads, "Forge of Gibbletrax."
  • Door to D5 A spiderweb is etched into this door. The inscription reads "Den of Itsy."
  • Door to D6 Etched into this door is the image of a scowling, bipedal hyenoid warrior. The door's inscription reads "Altar of Yeenoghu."

D2: Wasteland of Filth

A putrid stench hangs in this room. Gnawed bones, rotten food, and ancient junk litter the stone floor.

This room holds refuse discarded by the dungeon's denizens.

Treasure

As a Search action, a character can sift through the trash and make a 12 Wisdom (Perception) check. The first character to succeed on the check unearths five ivory urns. Each urn is worth 10 GP. Four of the urns are empty, but one contains a Potion of Healing and a tiny pewter statue of a two-headed demon worth 90 GP. A character who inspects the statue and succeeds on a 13 Intelligence (Religion) check recognizes the statue as an idol of the demon lord Demogorgon.

D3: Labyrinth of Doom

The torches along the walls of this maze begin to flicker, and a familiar disembodied voice says, "Many adventurers have met their demise in these corridors. Beware the fearsome minotaur!"

A spawn of Demogorgon feeds on its latest victim

Until recently, a bloodthirsty minotaur ruled this trap-filled labyrinth. However, an even more vicious creature—the spawn of Demogorgon, a demon lord—escaped the Vale of Shadows and slew the minotaur. The spawn is devouring the minotaur's corpse in the middle of the labyrinth.

Spear Traps

The labyrinth contains three spear traps triggered by pressure plates hidden in the floor, as denoted with a "T" on the Dungeon of Shadows map. Cobwebs and dust obscure the holes that house these spears.

Each spear trap has the following rules:

  • Detect and Disarm. As a Search action, a character can examine the walls and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, detecting the holes on a successful check. Alternatively, a character can take the Study action to inspect the floor and make a 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, detecting the pressure plate on a successful check.
  • Triggering the Trap. When a creature moves onto a trap's pressure plate for the first time on a turn, spears thrust out from the walls. Each creature on the pressure plate must succeed on a 13 Dexterity Saving Throw or be struck by a spear, taking 1d6 Piercing damage. The spears then retract, and the trap resets immediately.

Terror in the Maze

When the characters reach the center of the maze, read or paraphrase the following text:

The torches in this bloodstained corridor sputter erratically. A thin, sinewy creature with slimy, gray skin and elongated limbs crouches over a slain minotaur. The corpse squelches and snaps unsettlingly as the creature gorges on it. A small chest lies beside the mangled minotaur.

The Demogorgon Spawn continues devouring the minotaur for 1 minute or until it detects the characters. The spawn is Hostile [Attitude] toward all other creatures.

This encounter is pretty tough. Go easy on them... unless they're being ********, in which case you should give 'em hell.

To sneak past the spawn while it feeds, a character must succeed on a 13 Dexterity (Stealth) check. On a failed check, or if the characters otherwise disturb the spawn, it turns toward the adventurers. When that happens, read or paraphrase the following text:

The creature turns toward you, and its faceless head peels back to reveal five toothed, fleshy petals around a gaping mouth. It screeches and rushes toward you.

Roll Initiative!

The Demogorgon spawn fights until it is reduced to 25 Hit Points or fewer, at which point it retreats through the secret door to area S3 of the Shadow Dungeon (detailed later in this adventure). If the characters manage to defeat the Demogorgon spawn here, the adventure doesn't end; the characters still must find Flizzlebin to complete his quest.

If the characters don't disturb the spawn and aren't detected, the creature finishes its meal and then relocates to area S4 in the Shadow Dungeon.

Secret Door

A secret door (see "Dungeon Features") is set into the wall in the southeast corner of the labyrinth. It leads to area S3. Characters who witnessed the Demogorgon spawn use this secret door automatically succeed on checks to find the door.

Treasure

The chest in the middle of the labyrinth contains a Wand of Secrets and 25 GP.

D4: Forge of Gibbletrax

Clanging hammers ring out in this sweltering chamber. Three goblin smiths cluster around a glowing forge in the center of the room. The goblins sing in scratchy tones as they work:

"Deep within the Dungeon of Shadows,

We strengthen steel to slay the beasts.

Upside down in the Vale of Shadows,

Brave heroes delve to keep us free."

Blessed by a long-forgotten god, the Forge of Gibbletrax is a magic forge stewarded by three Goblin Warrior named Ble, Gib, and Trax. These smiths craft gear to defend against the dungeon's threats.

The goblins are initially Friendly [Attitude] toward the characters but defend themselves if necessary. If the characters approach the goblins peacefully, the goblins greet the characters warmly and ask what brings them to the dungeon.

Ble, Glib, and Trax usually keep to themselves, but they recently clashed with the gnolls in area D6, whose profane rituals threaten the sanctity of the forge. If the characters agree to end the gnolls' foul rites, the goblins vow to imbue the characters' weapons with the forge's magic.

Forge of Gibbletrax

The goblins' magical forge can temporarily infuse weapons and ammunition with immense heat. As a Bonus Action, a character can dip one weapon or piece of ammunition into the forge, coating it in a thin layer of molten ore. A creature that takes damage from the ore-coated weapon or ammunition takes an extra 1d6 Fire damage. Once coated, the weapon retains its heat for 10 minutes or until its damage is dealt, whichever comes first.

A character can benefit from the Forge of Gibbletrax only once, unless the goblins permit them to do so again. If all three goblins are slain or the forge is removed from this area, its magic ceases to function.

Three goblin smiths—Ble, Gib, and Trax—gleefully toil away at their magic forge while singing a work song

You can do this!

Sure, these smiths could have been dwarves, but that would've been BORING. Anyone can be a smith, just like anyone can be a Dungeon Master.

D5: Den of Itsy

Thick, sticky webs cover this once-regal chamber. Skeletons encased in cocoons hang from webs on the ceiling as grim warnings to all who enter.

A cobwebbed statue of an eight-foot-tall, armor-clad knight presides over the chamber. Before it is a stone pedestal, atop which rests a shimmering crystal spider roughly five feet in diameter. A fiery greatsword burns within the crystal spider's body, casting a warm, orange glow on the tangled nest.

  • DM Secret!. Don't reveal the Giant Spider yet. This monster is hiding.

This room is the nest of Itsy, a Giant Spider that preys on any who enter its lair. The Hostile [Attitude] spider clings to the ceiling, guarding the secret door and treasure in this room (detailed below). If a character opens the secret door or disturbs the crystal spider, Itsy begins combat.

Crystal Spider

The crystal spider is a Medium object with AC 13, HP 50, Resistance to Piercing and Slashing damage, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Destroying the crystal spider frees the treasure inside (detailed below).

Secret Door

Set into the east wall of this room is a secret door (see "Dungeon Features") that connects to area S5.

Statue

The statue depicts a knight in a gallant pose. As a Study action, a character can examine the statue and make a 12 Intelligence (Investigation) check. On a successful check, the character realizes the statue's base is unstable; a significant push could topple the statue.

As an action, a character within 5 feet of the statue can make a 10 Strength (Athletics) check to topple the statue into a space within 5 feet of it, doing so on a successful check. When the statue topples, each creature beneath it takes 4d6 Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition. The statue crumbles on impact, revealing a treasure hidden inside it (see "Treasure" below).

Webs

The web-filled areas are Difficult Terrain.

A creature that enters a web-filled area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a 12 Dexterity Saving Throw or have the Restrained condition. As an action, a creature Restrained by the webs can try to escape from them, doing so with a successful 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

Each 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect] of webs has AC 10; HP 7; Vulnerability to Fire damage; and Immunity to Piercing, Poison, and Psychic damage.

Treasure

Inside the statue is a heart-shaped emerald worth 30 GP. The sword encased in the crystal spider is a Flame Tongue Greatsword.

D6: Altar of Yeenoghu

In this square chamber, three hyenoid warriors kneel before an altar bearing a wicked-looking flail. Two of the creatures cackle maniacally as the third—the mangiest of the three who's nearly devoid of hair—chants, "Yeenoghu! Hear our laughter and let there be bloodshed and butchery!" The flail glows with sickly light.

These three Gnoll Warrior worship Yeenoghu, a merciless demon lord who delights in slaughter. The Hostile [Attitude] gnolls fight all other creatures on sight.

Completing the Ritual

If the characters don't interrupt the gnolls, they continue their ritual. After 1 minute, booming laughter erupts from the altar. Any creatures other than the gnolls in this area must make a 13 Constitution saving throw, taking 1d8 Thunder damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

After the ritual, the gnolls leave to battle the goblins in area D4. If the characters don't intervene, the gnolls overpower the goblins, and the Forge of Gibbletrax loses its magic forever.

Treasure

The flail on the altar is a +1 Flail.

Shadow Dungeon

Beneath the Dungeon of Shadows lies the Shadow Dungeon, a gloomy reflection of the dungeon that borders the Vale of Shadows. Though its chambers mirror the areas above, their contents differ, distorted by the eerie realm they border.

Finding Flizzlebin

To find Flizzlebin, the characters must defeat the Demogorgon spawn and any Hostile [Attitude] creatures in Flizzlebin's hiding spot (see the "Hide-and-Seek" section earlier in this adventure). When both conditions are met, the gnome appears to the characters; proceed to this adventure's conclusion.

If the characters reach Flizzlebin's hiding spot before they vanquish the Demogorgon spawn, read or paraphrase the following text:

"Ah! You found my hiding spot! But your work isn't done yet," says a familiar voice. "To claim your prize, you must slay the horrid creature that hunts me."

Flizzlebin doesn't bequeath his reward until the characters comply with his instructions. At your discretion, he might reveal the Demogorgon spawn's location—likely area S4.

Shadow Dungeon Features

The Shadow Dungeon has the following features:

  • Ceilings. The ceilings are 20 feet high in rooms and 10 feet high in passages.
  • Lighting. The dungeon is unlit. Area descriptions assume the characters have a light source or other means of seeing in Darkness. Bare iron sconces line the walls.
  • Doors and Secret Doors. Doors are unlocked and made of basalt. Secret doors manifest as spidery, elastic fissures that blend in with their surroundings and exude faint rays of natural light when opened. As a Search action, a character can examine a wall that contains a secret door and make a 15 Wisdom (Perception) check, noticing it on a successful check.

Shadow Dungeon Locations

The characters can enter and leave the Shadow Dungeon through the secret door that connects areas D3 and S3 or the secret door that connects areas D5 and S5. The following locations are keyed to the upside-down portion of the Dungeon of Shadows map.

S1: Chamber of Bad Choices

This eerie chamber has five stone doors, each bearing a vile image and inscription. A dead dwarf is slumped in a shadowy corner. The corpse clutches a torn sheet of parchment in its stiff hand. Near the dwarf, a stone staircase blocked by rubble ascends into darkness.

This room mirrors the Chamber of Choice (area D1). The corpse is that of a dwarf explorer who perished four days ago while searching for Flizzlebin. The dwarf was killed by an Undead shadow.

The dwarf's body is unnaturally thin, and its clothes look too big. A character can inspect the corpse and make a 12 Wisdom (Medicine) check. On a successful check, the character discerns the dwarf's life was sapped by a supernatural force.

The dwarf clutches a note. If the characters remove it from the corpse, show the players the Dungeon Warning Handout. After the characters read the note, a Shadow rises from the dwarf's corpse and begins combat.

Dungeon Warning Handout

Doors

Each of the five doors is adorned with a relief sculpture and an inscription as follows:

  • Door to S2 (Urn). This door bears the image of an urn wrapped in ink-black vines. The inscription reads "Wasteland of Filthy Vines."
  • Door to S3 (Labyrinth). This door's relief depicts a fungal maze. The inscription reads, "Labyrinth of Gloom."
  • Door to S4 (Spiked Anvil). In this door's relief, a shadowy figure looms over a spiked anvil. The inscription reads, "Forge of Annihilation."
  • Door to S5 (Web). A black spiderweb is etched into this door. The inscription reads "Den of Bitsy."
  • Door to S6 (Hand and Eye). A desiccated hand holding an eye decorates this door. Deep scratches make the inscription illegible.

Staircase

The staircase, blocked by rubble, leads to the Vale of Shadows. That realm and its contents are beyond the scope of this adventure, but you can flesh them out as you see fit. Otherwise, the staircase is impassible.

S2: Wasteland of Filthy Vines

Slithering black vines squirm along the floor of this trash-filled room.

This room mirrors the Wasteland of Filth (area D2). The floor is Difficult Terrain.

Treasure

The first character to sift through the trash and succeed on a 12 Wisdom (Perception) check unearths five cracked urns hewn from black granite. The urns are worthless. Four of the urns are empty, but one contains a Potion of Healing and a glass eye with an emerald pupil worth 10 GP.

S3: Labyrinth of Gloom

Clouds of spores drift throughout this stone labyrinth. The maze is overgrown with fungi and foot-tall mushrooms that sprout from the walls and floor.

This stone maze mirrors the Labyrinth of Doom (area D3). The maze is home to toxic plants and four Shrieker Fungus. Two Hostile [Attitude] Myconid Adult also roam the maze, fighting any non-Plants they encounter.

If the shriekers sound off, the myconids investigate the disturbance. The shriekers don't shriek if the myconids come within 30 feet of them.

Secret Door

A secret door (see "Shadow Dungeon Features") is set into the wall near the southeast corner of the maze. It leads to area D3.

Spore Traps

The labyrinth contains three spore traps—swollen plant bulbs that exhale puffs of toxic spores—triggered by stepping on pressure plates of inflated mushrooms. These traps are marked on Dungeon of Shadows map with a "T." The fungus-infested walls obscure the bulbs that spray these spores.

Each spore trap has the following rules:

  • Detect and Disarm. As a Study action, a character can examine the walls and make a 15 Intelligence (Nature) check, identifying the toxic bulbs on a successful check. Alternatively, a character can take the Study action to inspect the floor and make a 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check, identifying the fungal pressure plate on a successful check. Trimming the stems that connect the bulbs to the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.
  • Triggering the Trap. When a creature moves onto a pressure plate for the first time on a turn, the bulbs spray toxic spores that fill a 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect] centered on the pressure plate. Each creature in the Cube must succeed on a 13 Constitution Saving Throw or have the Poisoned condition for 1 hour. The trap resets immediately.

Treasure

A dilapidated chest in the middle of the labyrinth contains a broken wand and 25 GP. The wand is useless.

S4: Forge of Annihilation

An unholy forge dominates this grim chamber. Caustic fumes waft from its icy hearth, which swirls with a faintly glowing, pale-green slurry. Skulls bob along the liquid's surface.

This room mirrors the Forge of Gibbletrax (area D4). If the Demogorgon spawn survived its previous encounter with the characters (see area D3), it lurks here. Read or paraphrase the following text:

A familiar, horrible creature—the same creature you encountered in the labyrinth above—rises from the shadow of the forge. It unfurls its faceless head once more and chitters in anticipation.

Roll Initiative!

The Demogorgon Spawn fights to the death.

Forge of Annihilation

Unlike the goblins' blessed forge in the dungeon above, this forge is a cursed apparatus capable only of destruction. The Forge of Annihilation causes living creatures to wither and die. As a Study action, a character can inspect the forge and make a 13 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a successful check, the character identifies the eldritch hazard and the threat it poses.

A creature that enters the forge for the first time or starts its turn there must make a 15 Constitution Saving Throw, taking 4d8 Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

The Forge of Annihilation—a sinister reflection of the Forge of Gibbletrax—looms within the Shadow Dungeon

S5: Den of Bitsy

A statue of an eight-foot-tall knight with a horned, crimson helm stands in this chamber, which is covered in thick, black webs. Atop an altar in the center of the room, a massive spider with dripping fangs wraps a dead elf in webs.

Humanoid-shaped cocoons—the arachnid's ghastly larder—hang throughout the chamber.

This room mirrors the Den of Itsy (area D5). It belongs to Bitsy, an equally territorial Giant Spider. Bitsy fights the characters on sight.

Secret Door

Set into the east wall in this room is a secret door (see "Shadow Dungeon Features") that connects to area D5.

Statue

The statue depicts a knight with a menacing helm. As a Study action, a character can examine the statue and make a 12 Intelligence (Investigation) check. On a successful check, the character realizes the statue's base is unstable; a significant push could topple the statue.

As an action, a character within 5 feet of the statue can make a 10 Strength (Athletics) check to topple the statue into a space within 5 feet of it, doing so on a successful check. When the statue topples, each creature beneath it takes 4d6 Bludgeoning damage and has the Prone condition. The statue crumbles on impact, revealing treasure within (see "Treasure" below), but its helm remains intact.

Webs

The web-filled areas are Difficult Terrain.

A creature that enters a web-filled area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a 12 Dexterity Saving Throw or have the Restrained condition. As an action, a creature Restrained by the webs can try to escape from them, doing so with a successful 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

Each 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect] of webs has AC 10; HP 7; Vulnerability to Fire damage; and Immunity to Piercing, Poison, and Psychic damage.

Treasure

The statue's helmet is a crimson Dread Helm that resembles the head of a horned devil. Inside the statue is a heart-shaped black tourmaline worth 30 GP.

S6: Altar of Vecna

Low fog pervades this eerily quiet chamber. A stone altar rises from the center of the floor. Atop the altar, a dismembered hand grasps an hourglass half-filled with black sand and adorned with bone spindles. The sand defies gravity, flowing to the top bulb.

This room mirrors the Altar of Yeenoghu (area D6), but this altar honors evil of a viler caliber.

The first character to inspect the hourglass hears the sound of a ticking clock, followed by a baleful chime. The hourglass then cracks, and the sand spills out, revealing a mummified eye within the lower bulb. No other character hears the sound.

Afterward, a character can examine the altar's contents and make a 12 Intelligence (Religion) check. On a successful check, the character recognizes the hand and the eye as the symbol of Vecna, a powerful lich feared throughout Greyhawkins. The hourglass is a ceremonial object used by members of Vecna's cult to symbolize the lich's dreaded—and inevitable—return.
