title: Devil, Metal, Die!
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Devil, Metal, Die!

An Adventure for Level 3 Characters

This adventure is designed to fill one or two sessions of play.

If you aren't using the Map of Greyhawkins, it can begin in any tavern before descending into the Nine Hells.

Key Plot Points

This information is key to the adventure's story:

  • Plot Point 1. Dardew invites the characters to compete in the Hellfire Games. If they accept, they're transported to the Hellfire Dome.
  • Plot Point 2. In the Hellfire Dome, the characters face off against devils, demons, and a dragon unlike any other.
  • Plot Point 3. Spectators shower the characters with gold throughout the competition. If a character falls in battle, Dardew intercedes and offers them the chance to rise and fight again as part of an infernal pact.
  • Plot Point 4. The characters either complete all the challenges or die trying. Any survivors are inducted into the Hellfire Club.

DM Preparation

Before running the adventure, prepare as follows:

  • Step 1. Read the "Adventure Background" and "Deal with the Devil" sections.
  • Step 2. Familiarize yourself with the Infernal Contract Handout and the Hellfire Dome map.
  • Step 3. Familiarize yourself with the creatures in this adventure, which are as follows:
  • 1 Barbed Devil
  • 1 Bearded Devil
  • 5 Cultist of Demogorgon
  • Dardew
  • 5 Demobat
  • 1 Demodragon
  • 1 Demogorgon Spawn
  • 6 Dretch
  • 3 Gnoll Warrior
  • 2 Hell Hound
  • 1 Imp Trickster
  • 1 Medusa
  • Step 4. Familiarize yourself with the Magic Items in this adventure, which are as follows:
  • Adamantine Breastplate
  • Potion of Healing
  • Spiked Shield

This is it: the final trial to see who's worthy of joining Hellfire! This deadly gauntlet separates the wheat from the chaff, real heroes from would-be plunderers. Make sure everyone can make it to game night. If they skip this one, they're OUT. Lure them with the promise of epic adventure, priceless treasures, and CERTAIN DEATH.

Oh, and snacks. Bring those, too.

Player Assistance

You can simplify the DM's role by having the a player handle tasks typically assigned to the DM. Before play begins, see if a player would like to be the Rules Consultant. That player references the D&D Beyond Basic Rules as needed.

  • Monster Wranglers. Whenever the characters encounter Hostile [Attitude] monsters, one or two players can run those monsters using the referenced stat blocks. (If you have two players doing this, they can take turns.)
  • Rules Consultant. One player references the D&D Beyond Basic Rules as needed.
Within the Hellfire Dome, Dardew welcomes an audience of roisterous fiends to the Hellfire Games

Adventure Background

From the fires of the Nine Hells rises the infamous Hellfire Dome, a diabolical arena where contestants of ill repute vie for gold and glory. Death, betrayal, and priceless treasures await those who endure the lethal games in the dome, which are spectated by an audience of disorderly fiends.

Contestants must rely on strength and wits to overcome the diabolical gauntlet that awaits them in the dome. The last and greatest of these trials is a showdown with the Demodragon: a wretched, two-headed terror created by Demogorgon, the Prince of Demons. Those who slay the Demodragon depart the Nine Hells as wealthy champions.

Winners are also inducted into the Hellfire Club, an exclusive association of infernal origin respected by devils of every rank. Members of the Hellfire Club have a reputation for being tough, fearless, and above all—totally metal.

Every six years, the Hellfire Dome opens its doors to non-Fiends, allowing them to compete in a series of infernal challenges. Dardew the Banished, a cambion with aspirations of grandeur, invites the characters to compete in the arena. If victorious, the characters will be crowned members of the legendary Hellfire Club, and Dardew will rise in the fiery ranks. However, if the characters lose, they might forfeit their souls.

Dardew the Banished

This year's master of ceremonies for the Hellfire Games is a music-loving fiend named Dardew the Banished. A lowly cambion, Dardew hopes to ascend the ranks of the Nine Hells through panache and showmanship, impressing powerful devils in the audience with an unforgettable performance. He believes the characters are his ticket to fame.

Deal with the Devil

Few survive the Hellfire Dome in one piece, but those who make deals with devils have a better chance at making it out alive. Early deaths among contestants can make for an underwhelming display, and Dardew can't afford for this year's Hellfire Games to disappoint.

To give the characters an edge in the arena, Dardew has arranged a special contract to keep them fighting beyond the brink of death. Still, no fiend can resist corrupting a mortal soul, especially one that belongs to a good-hearted adventurer. The characters would be wise to consider the contract's fine print before they sign.

Souls for sale! Death is a part of the game, but it doesn't have to be the end. And in this adventure, it can be fun for everyone involved! Celebrate players who push their luck and amplify this great, bloody, gladiatorial spectacle. You can always give them their characters' souls back later... if you're a pushover.

Infernal Contract

Whenever a character drops to 0 Hit Points in the Hellfire Dome, Dardew extends an infernal contract to that character. This event takes place outside the Initiative order, which resumes after the character accepts or declines Dardew's offer.

Read or paraphrase the following text:

The scene around you freezes as Dardew appears and unfurls a lengthy contract. "I've got a good feeling about you. How would you like to keep going?"

Show that player the Infernal Contract Handout and ask them if their character agrees to the following terms:

  • Defying Death. When you drop to 0 Hit Points while in the Hellfire Dome—including when you are first offered this contract—you can roll any number of d6s (minimum of 3d6) and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll's total (no action required). If you roll a 6 on three or more of these dice, you also forfeit your soul and can't benefit from the contract in this way again.
  • Forfeiting Your Soul. If you forfeit your soul, it becomes the property of Dardew the Banished on your death.
  • Voiding the Contract. As a Magic action, Dardew or an archdevil can void this contract, returning any forfeited souls to their previous owners. Destroying the contract or its arbiter doesn't void the agreement.

If the character accepts these terms, they sign the contract. Dardew then collects the contract and vanishes in a cloud of brimstone. Dardew reappears to offer the same contract to any character who drops to 0 Hit Points while in the Hellfire Dome, even if the character previously rejected the contract.

This is Hellfire.

If the characters reject Dardew, your players are either scaredy cats or a bunch of *****. Either way, put on your favorite mix and wait 'em out. They'll come to their senses eventually.

It's D&D or bust.

Beginning the Adventure

When the players are ready to begin the adventure, read or paraphrase the following text:

You sit in an unremarkable tavern somewhere in Greyhawkins when, in a burst of brimstone, a winged, red-skinned fiend with a mane of curly hair and a boyish smile appears. He lands atop one of the tables with an exaggerated bow.

"Greetings, mortal adventurers. My name is Dardew. I hope I'm not interrupting your meal," he says coyly.

"I've come to invite you to compete in the Hellfire Games. I've been watching you for some time now, and I believe you just might have what it takes to join the esteemed Hellfire Club. Care to play the devils' game?"

Dardew has come to recruit the characters for the Hellfire Games. He is Indifferent [Attitude] toward the party—but still charming—and shares the following information about the competition:

  • Hellfire Games. The Hellfire Games are a sexennial competition in which contestants battle for prestige, treasure, and induction into the exclusive Hellfire Club.
  • Hellfire Club. The Hellfire Club is an invite-only club whose members include epic heroes, high-ranking devils, and figures of legend.

Hellfire Dome. The games are held in the Hellfire Dome, an arena far from Greyhawkins; Dardew is this year's host and can take the characters there.

If the characters ask about the risk, Dardew explains that while the Hellfire Games are dangerous, the characters have nothing to worry about. He has prepared a special contract to help the characters cheat death (see "Deal with the Devil"), though he doesn't delve into specifics.

Accepting the Invitation

If the characters accept Dardew's invitation, he magically transports them to the Hellfire Dome. Read or paraphrase the following text:

"That's the spirit!" Dardew laughs and claps his hands, and a cloud of red smoke engulfs you.

The characters begin the games in area H1 of the Hellfire Dome.

Declining the Invitation

If the characters decline, read or paraphrase:

"Hmm, not what I expected. Oh, well! Maybe next time." Dardew shrugs and disappears with a puff of smoke.

At your discretion, Dardew might return later to reissue his invitation, perhaps offering an important insight or piece of information in return for the characters' participation.

Hellfire Dome

Devils prize competition, treachery, and power, so they created the Hellfire Dome, a gauntlet of deadly scenarios designed to feature all three. These challenges take place in a volcanic pit on Avernus, the first layer of the Nine Hells. Just outside the arid dome lies an endless wasteland razed in the Blood War, an eternal conflict between devils and demons.

The Hellfire Dome is a multistory arena hewn from obsidian. A massive dome forged from infernal steel covers the arena, shielding it from meteors that fall from Avernus's skies. Beneath the dome, an infernal steel cage prevents contestants from escaping.

Thousands of devils gather to watch the Hellfire Games. These rowdy onlookers sometimes cast coins into the pit, showering contenders with gold. Unpopular contestants occasionally receive a ball of flame hurled by a disgruntled fiend.

Refer to the Hellfire Dome map and note that the players begin in the center of area H1. Don't reveal the rest of the map's contents yet, as it is not not initially visible to the characters.

Hellfire Dome Features

The Hellfire Dome has the following features:

  • Ambiance. The arena is dry and oppressively hot, and it reeks of blood and brimstone. The audience roars with cheers and howls.
  • Ceilings. Aside from the dome over the arena, the Hellfire Dome has no ceilings. An indestructible cage 60 feet above the pit separates contestants from the audience.
  • Lighting. Unless otherwise specified, areas in the dome are in Bright Light.
  • Portals. Each of the lettered portals on Hellfire Dome map is a gateway of harmless fire linked to another area in the arena. A creature that enters a portal emerges within 5 feet of the portal with the matching letter on Hellfire Dome map or in the nearest unoccupied space.

Dungeon Locations

The following locations are keyed to the Hellfire Dome map. The map also shows the locations of characters and monsters in the tunnels.

H1: Hellfire Arena

As the smoke clears, you find yourself in a pit within a hellish arena. The temperature is oppressively hot, and the air stinks of sulfur. Thousands of devils leer down at you from rows of seating above a twisted cage of infernal steel. Diabolical music fills the arena.

You stand on a raised platform inscribed with a pentagram. Red flames burn in five braziers, one at each of the star's points.

Dardew flies over the pit. His voice booms out, quieting the din. "Welcome, one and all, to the Hellfire Dome! Prepare yourselves for a night of death, betrayal, and vile spectacle." The audience erupts in thunderous applause.

"I present to you our latest contenders: group five hundred twenty-seven! Will they survive to become the Hellfire Club's newest initiates? Only time will tell, but we wish them luck. Let the Hellfire Games begin!"

Suddenly, five eyeless, flying demons burst from the fiery braziers.

The five Demobat fight to the death. Whenever the characters vanquish a Demobat, the audience rewards them (see "Treasure" below). Once the characters defeat the bats, five blazing portals appear along the arena's walls.

Dardew then floats down and congratulates the characters on completing their first challenge. He informs them that only after they have completed at least two more challenges can they proceed through the east portal to their final test (area H7). Dardew doesn't reveal what lies beyond any of the portals.

  • Portals. Five portals in the arena lead to the following locations:
  • Portal A. Portal A leads to area H4.
  • Portal B. Portal B leads to area H3.
  • Portal C. Portal C leads to area H7. The portal doesn't function until the characters have completed challenges in at least two other areas.
  • Portal D. Portal D leads to area H5.
  • Portal E. Portal E leads to area H2.

Each portal initially functions as a one-way door, preventing reentry until the characters have completed the challenge in the destination area.

Treasure

Each time a character kills a Demobat, the audience throws 50 GP into this area.

Dardew amuses a cultist of Demogorgon during a trivia round of Fiend Feud

H2: Fiend Feud

Dardew hovers impatiently over this room, which features two rusty, wrought-iron podiums that resemble corroded coffins. Five masked cultists stand behind one of the podiums, while the other is vacant.

"It's that time again!" Dardew announces to the devils above. "Are you ready for another game of Fiend Feud?" The audience cheers. "Contestants, take your places." Dardew clears his throat and gestures to the empty podium.

This challenge is called Fiend Feud, a trivia game of brains and bloodshed where two teams compete for fame, fortune—and their lives. The opposing team consists of five Cultist of Demogorgon who are Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters. Dardew acts as host.

Once the characters take their places behind the podium, the game begins.

  • Playing Fiend Feud. Fiend Feud is a trivia game with three rounds and a mostly arbitrary points system. The game's rules are as follows:
  • Trivia Questions. Each round, Dardew asks the characters one question from the Fiend Feud Questions table, rerolling duplicates. These questions test player knowledge as much as character knowledge. The player characters are allowed to briefly deliberate before giving their response. If they answer the question correctly, their team receives 1 point.
  • Chance to Steal. If the characters answer a question incorrectly, the opposing team has a chance answer the question, receiving 1 point if they answer it correctly. The cultists are well-versed in occult lore and answer any such questions correctly, but they know little about anything else and get those questions wrong. The cultists know the answers to questions 1, 4, and 6 in the Fiend Feud Questions table.
  • Bonus Round. After three rounds of trivia, both teams can earn bonus points by killing members of the opposing team. Have everyone roll Initiative. For each opposing team member they slay, a team earns 1 point.

The game ends when only one team remains.

If you really want to run a certain encounter, you can just have whichever portal the characters go through lead to that area. It's an old DM trick I like to call "the invisible railroad."

Fiend Feud Questions
1d6QuestionAnswer
1What vile lich is missing one eye and one hand?Vecna
2What creatures love brains but loathe zombies?Mind flayers
3Which vampire lord rules over the land of Barovia?Count Strahd von Zarovich
4Which demon lord is the self-styled Prince of Demons?Demogorgon
5Which warrior severed the hand of a famous lich?Kas
6Which archdevil rules over all the Nine Hells?Asmodeus

At the DM's discretion, a character can take the Study action to make a 15 Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) check to know the answer to a question, learning the correct answer on a successful check.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Correct Answers. Whenever a character correctly answers a question, the audience throws 10 GP into this area.
  • Slaying Cultists. Whenever a character slays a cultist, the audience throws 25 GP into this area.
  • Winning the Game. If the characters win Fiend Feud, the audience showers them with 150 GP.

H3: Demonic Incursion

This fetid chamber holds a bubbling well of brownish sludge. In front of the well, a devil stands poised for battle. Glaive in hand, the devil sports a writhing beard of barbed, snakelike appendages.

"Fight well alongside me, maggots," it spits, "Or I'll stick you like the smelly flesh bags you are!" Just then, the well burps up six squealing demons, each more hideous than the last.

An unseen creature whispers in your ear. "Kill the demons, then kill this devil—make it look like an accident, and you'll be rewarded. You have my word!"

A dretch bursts forth from a demonic well
  • DM Secret!. Don't reveal the Imp Trickster yet. This monster is invisible.

Six Dretch erupt from the well. The Hostile [Attitude] demons fight the characters and the Bearded Devil, which is initially Indifferent [Attitude] toward the party and fights alongside them. Once all six dretches have been slain, the challenge is complete, and the portal to area H1 reopens.

A treacherous Imp Trickster with the Invisible condition watches the battle unfold. The imp loathes the bearded devil and wishes it dead but is Indifferent [Attitude] toward the characters. During the battle, the imp encourages characters to turn on the bearded devil when the last dretch falls.

The Devil You Don't Know

The bearded devil is an overbearing grunt who barks orders at the characters and scolds any who defy its commands. Whenever a character slays a demon, the bearded devil loudly takes credit for the kill.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating the Bearded Devil. If a character kills the bearded devil, the imp turns visible and gives them 200 GP.
  • Defeating Dretches. Each time a character kills a dretch, the audience throws 50 GP into this area.
  • Defeating the Imp. If a character kills the Imp Trickster, the bearded devil thanks the characters for eliminating "the spy" and gives them 10 GP.

H4: Sanctuary of Yeenoghu

Three mangy, hyenoid fiends conduct a ritual in this wicked sanctuary. In the center of the chamber, a giant, wicked-looking flail spins and stops at unpredictable intervals, violently swinging its three spiked heads.

Two of the creatures cackle maliciously as the third—completely hairless—chants, "Yeenoghu! Deliver us from this wretched game so we may spill blood in your name!"

Three Gnoll Warrior beseech the demon lord Yeenoghu for aid in this sanctuary. They are Hostile [Attitude] toward all other creatures and rush them on sight.

These are the same gnolls from the Dungeon of Shadows (see "The Vanishing Gnome"). They have since died and made their way to the Hellfire Dome. If the characters fought them previously, the gnolls recognize them and greet them accordingly:

The gnolls visibly seethe with hatred. "You again?!" shouts the hairless gnoll. "Heretics! How dare you come here and interrupt our ritual a second time!"

The gnolls fight to the death (again).

Flail

The spinning flail is embedded in the ground between the gnolls. Each round on Initiative count 10 (losing Initiative ties), the flail's three heads crash to the ground. Each creature within 10 feet of the flail must succeed on a 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 Bludgeoning damage and have the Prone condition. The flail doesn't harm the gnolls.

The flail has AC 18, HP 40, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. If the flail is destroyed, it stops spinning, and the audience roars in jubilation.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating Gnolls. Each time a character kills a gnoll, the audience throws 100 GP into this area.
  • Destroying the Flail. If a character destroys the flail, the audience throws 200 GP into this area.

H5: Infernal Court

A judge with a nest of snakes for hair and wearing crimson robes presides over this infernal court. Two short podiums rest before the judge's bench, an imposing monument of black marble flanked by two snarling hounds; flames drip from the hounds' jaws. A lone imp perches atop one of the podiums. It snickers as you enter.

Nine petrified jurors with frightened expressions fill a juror's box to the north. The judge calls the court to order. "Order in the court!" the judge demands. "The accused have finally decided to join us—late and without representation. How do you plead?"

The judge is Yudith Duboix, a no-nonsense Medusa. Judge Deboix is Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters, who have just entered their own trial. Two Hell Hound ferociously obey the judge's commands.

The trial proceeds through arraignment, statements, and sentencing, as detailed in the following sections. The characters can either represent themselves or allow the Imp Trickster, an unlicensed attorney, to provide them with bad-faith representation.

The jury is composed of adventurers petrified by Judge Deboix. If the characters try to fight the court instead, they might be similarly turned to stone, in which case Dardew can amend his contract (see "Infernal Contract" earlier in this adventure) to also remove the Petrified condition.

  • Arraignment. After the characters' plea, Judge Duboix summarizes the charges against them, which might include but aren't limited to the following:
  • Arson. A character is charged with arson if they've ever set anything on fire, including torches.
  • Failure to Appear. A character is charged with failure to appear if their player has ever arrived late to a game session.
  • Murder. A character is charged with murder if they've ever slain a creature in combat.
  • Thievery. A character is charged with thievery if they've ever stolen property, including gold or items found in a dungeon or taken from the dead.
  • Trespassing. A character is charged with trespassing if they've ever entered a location, including a dungeon, without permission.

At your discretion, other offenses might be worthy of a charge in this kangaroo court.

Statements

The characters can confer and give a statement in their defense. A character can try to convince Judge Duboix of the party's innocence and make a 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. On a successful check, Judge Duboix finds the party not guilty and dismisses the characters from the court. On a failed check (or if the characters chose to let the imp represent them), Judge Duboix rules against the party and moves to sentencing.

If the party is found not guilty, the challenge is considered complete, and the portal to area H1 reopens.

Judge Yudith Duboix, a stone-cold medusa judge, demands order in the infernal court

Sentencing

Judge Duboix's sentencing is harsh and swift. If the party is found guilty, the medusa sentences the characters to 1,000 years in prison. The judge then orders the hell hounds to escort the characters to the infernal prison (area H6) for detainment. If the characters refuse, the hell hounds leap into battle. Judge Duboix defends itself as necessary but otherwise abstains from combat. If both hounds are slain, Judge Duboix surrenders and overturns the previous verdict.

If the characters comply with sentencing and later return to this area, the courtroom is empty, and the portal to area H1 reopens.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating Hell Hounds. Each time a character kills a hound, the audience throws 200 GP into this area.
  • Defeating Judge Duboix. If Judge Duboix dies, the audience throws 2,000 GP into this area.
  • Innocent Verdict. If the party is found innocent, the audience throws 100 GP into this area.

H6: Infernal Prison

A devil covered in sharp barbs patrols this open-air cell block. The devil rattles its tail against the bars of the six cages, laughing cruelly at the prisoners. A key hangs around the devil's neck.

The warden of this prison is a masochistic Barbed Devil named Khaos, the Bringer of Pain. Khaos is Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters. When they enter, the devil grunts and points them to the biggest cage (cage 1), attacking any who refuse to enter. Khaos then returns to marching up and down the block.

Khaos enjoys catching escaped prisoners and breaking their spirits and bodies. The devil doesn't confiscate inmates' equipment and pretends not to notice if they try to free themselves or one another. Khaos doesn't pursue runaways beyond this area.

Cages

Khaos wears the key to these six locked cages. As a Utilize action, a character can try to pick a cage's lock using Thieves' Tools, doing so with a successful 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The check is made with Disadvantage if the character is trying to pick the lock from inside the cage.

Alternatively, a character can try to goad Khaos into unlocking their cage. As an Influence action, a character can taunt the barbed devil and make a 13 Charisma (Performance) check. On a successful check, Khaos unlocks the door, enters the cage, and strikes that character to teach them a lesson.

The cage's contents are as follows:

  • Cage 1 contains only a bench chained to the wall.
  • Cage 2 contains a Demogorgon Spawn captured on the battlefields of Avernus. The spawn is Hostile [Attitude] toward all other creatures and tries to tear them limb from limb if freed from its cell.
  • Cage 3 is empty.
  • Cage 4 contains a human Cultist of Demogorgon who warns any who address her that the "Sibilant Beast" will consume them all. The Hostile [Attitude] cultist fights any who enter her cell.
  • Cage 5 contains an Imp Trickster playing a harmonica. The imp is Indifferent [Attitude] toward the characters but aids them in combat in this area if freed.
  • Cage 6 is empty.

If a character escapes their cage or frees one of the other imprisoned creatures, Khaos brays with malevolent laughter and fights the escapee.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating Khaos. If a character kills Khaos, the audience throws 2,000 GP into this area.
  • Defeating the Demogorgon Spawn. If a character kills the Demogorgon Spawn, the audience throws 150 GP into this area.

H7: Demodragon Lair

Dardew has tilted the odds in the characters' favor. When they enter this area, each character magically gains the benefits of finishing a Short Rest. Then, read or paraphrase the following text:

A river of molten lava flows through this scorched lair. Crumbling rubble, dried viscera, and cracked bones litter the ground, a barren landscape marred by past battles.

The earth trembles as a massive abomination with a sickly gray hide, razor-sharp claws, and two faceless heads rises from a mound of glittering treasure. It stretches its wide, leathery wings and unfurls its heads to reveal two gaping maws of toothed, fleshy petals. The behemoth bellows two bone-chilling roars.

Roll initiative!

The final challenge in the Hellfire Games is the Demodragon, an abomination that has slaughtered scores of contestants. The Demodragon is Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters and fights to the death.

  • Lava. Rivers of lava flow throughout this area, as shown on the map. A creature that enters the lava for the first time on a turn or starts its turn in the lava takes 6d10 fire damage.

Treasure

The Demodragon's hoard contains the following: an Adamantine Breastplate, a Spiked Shield, a Potion of Healing, and 2,420 GP.

The Demodragon rouses from its slumber to devour foolhardy contestants

Conclusion

The Hellfire Games conclude when the characters vanquish the Demodragon or die trying. If the characters defeat the Demodragon, read or paraphrase the following text:

With an earthshaking crash, the Demodragon collapses dead before you. The crowd goes wild.

Dardew soars overhead. "Wow! What a show!" he crows. "Friends and fiends, please join me in welcoming our latest Hellfire champions!"

He flies toward you and says quietly, "Adventurers, now would be a great time to take a bow. You've earned it."

In addition to the treasure they collected in the Hellfire Dome, the characters earn the following rewards for winning the Hellfire Games:

  • Hellfire Club Membership. Dardew invites characters to join the Hellfire Club. If they accept his invitation, they each receive a pendant worth 50 GP. The pendant depicts the face of a red devil flanked by a flail and flaming sword.
  • Hellfire Hall of Fame. The characters are inducted into the Hellfire Hall of Fame. Their names are recorded forever in the annals of infernal history alongside other legendary heroes and villains.
  • Voiding the Infernal Contract. If any character entered into an infernal contract with Dardew (see "Infernal Contract" earlier in this adventure), Dardew voids the contract.

When the characters are ready to leave the Nine Hells, Dardew magically returns them to Greyhawkins. Before he departs, Dardew thanks them for the magnificent performance.

Congratulations.

Hellfire is officially in your hands.

You should take a bow, too. Being a DM can feel overwhelming sometimes, but know this: You're not alone. I promise. If you ever need a pep talk, I'm just a phone call away. Save me a seat at your table. I'll be back to see what you've done with the place.

title: Adventure Background
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Adventure Background

From the fires of the Nine Hells rises the infamous Hellfire Dome, a diabolical arena where contestants of ill repute vie for gold and glory. Death, betrayal, and priceless treasures await those who endure the lethal games in the dome, which are spectated by an audience of disorderly fiends.

Contestants must rely on strength and wits to overcome the diabolical gauntlet that awaits them in the dome. The last and greatest of these trials is a showdown with the Demodragon: a wretched, two-headed terror created by Demogorgon, the Prince of Demons. Those who slay the Demodragon depart the Nine Hells as wealthy champions.

Winners are also inducted into the Hellfire Club, an exclusive association of infernal origin respected by devils of every rank. Members of the Hellfire Club have a reputation for being tough, fearless, and above all—totally metal.

Every six years, the Hellfire Dome opens its doors to non-Fiends, allowing them to compete in a series of infernal challenges. Dardew the Banished, a cambion with aspirations of grandeur, invites the characters to compete in the arena. If victorious, the characters will be crowned members of the legendary Hellfire Club, and Dardew will rise in the fiery ranks. However, if the characters lose, they might forfeit their souls.

Dardew the Banished

This year's master of ceremonies for the Hellfire Games is a music-loving fiend named Dardew the Banished. A lowly cambion, Dardew hopes to ascend the ranks of the Nine Hells through panache and showmanship, impressing powerful devils in the audience with an unforgettable performance. He believes the characters are his ticket to fame.

title: Deal with the Devil
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Deal with the Devil

Few survive the Hellfire Dome in one piece, but those who make deals with devils have a better chance at making it out alive. Early deaths among contestants can make for an underwhelming display, and Dardew can't afford for this year's Hellfire Games to disappoint.

To give the characters an edge in the arena, Dardew has arranged a special contract to keep them fighting beyond the brink of death. Still, no fiend can resist corrupting a mortal soul, especially one that belongs to a good-hearted adventurer. The characters would be wise to consider the contract's fine print before they sign.

Souls for sale! Death is a part of the game, but it doesn't have to be the end. And in this adventure, it can be fun for everyone involved! Celebrate players who push their luck and amplify this great, bloody, gladiatorial spectacle. You can always give them their characters' souls back later... if you're a pushover.

Infernal Contract

Whenever a character drops to 0 Hit Points in the Hellfire Dome, Dardew extends an infernal contract to that character. This event takes place outside the Initiative order, which resumes after the character accepts or declines Dardew's offer.

Read or paraphrase the following text:

The scene around you freezes as Dardew appears and unfurls a lengthy contract. "I've got a good feeling about you. How would you like to keep going?"

Show that player the Infernal Contract Handout and ask them if their character agrees to the following terms:

  • Defying Death. When you drop to 0 Hit Points while in the Hellfire Dome—including when you are first offered this contract—you can roll any number of d6s (minimum of 3d6) and regain a number of Hit Points equal to the roll's total (no action required). If you roll a 6 on three or more of these dice, you also forfeit your soul and can't benefit from the contract in this way again.
  • Forfeiting Your Soul. If you forfeit your soul, it becomes the property of Dardew the Banished on your death.
  • Voiding the Contract. As a Magic action, Dardew or an archdevil can void this contract, returning any forfeited souls to their previous owners. Destroying the contract or its arbiter doesn't void the agreement.

If the character accepts these terms, they sign the contract. Dardew then collects the contract and vanishes in a cloud of brimstone. Dardew reappears to offer the same contract to any character who drops to 0 Hit Points while in the Hellfire Dome, even if the character previously rejected the contract.

This is Hellfire.

If the characters reject Dardew, your players are either scaredy cats or a bunch of *****. Either way, put on your favorite mix and wait 'em out. They'll come to their senses eventually.

It's D&D or bust.

title: Beginning the Adventure
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Beginning the Adventure

When the players are ready to begin the adventure, read or paraphrase the following text:

You sit in an unremarkable tavern somewhere in Greyhawkins when, in a burst of brimstone, a winged, red-skinned fiend with a mane of curly hair and a boyish smile appears. He lands atop one of the tables with an exaggerated bow.

"Greetings, mortal adventurers. My name is Dardew. I hope I'm not interrupting your meal," he says coyly.

"I've come to invite you to compete in the Hellfire Games. I've been watching you for some time now, and I believe you just might have what it takes to join the esteemed Hellfire Club. Care to play the devils' game?"

Dardew has come to recruit the characters for the Hellfire Games. He is Indifferent [Attitude] toward the party—but still charming—and shares the following information about the competition:

  • Hellfire Games. The Hellfire Games are a sexennial competition in which contestants battle for prestige, treasure, and induction into the exclusive Hellfire Club.
  • Hellfire Club. The Hellfire Club is an invite-only club whose members include epic heroes, high-ranking devils, and figures of legend.

Hellfire Dome. The games are held in the Hellfire Dome, an arena far from Greyhawkins; Dardew is this year's host and can take the characters there.

If the characters ask about the risk, Dardew explains that while the Hellfire Games are dangerous, the characters have nothing to worry about. He has prepared a special contract to help the characters cheat death (see "Deal with the Devil"), though he doesn't delve into specifics.

Accepting the Invitation

If the characters accept Dardew's invitation, he magically transports them to the Hellfire Dome. Read or paraphrase the following text:

"That's the spirit!" Dardew laughs and claps his hands, and a cloud of red smoke engulfs you.

The characters begin the games in area H1 of the Hellfire Dome.

Declining the Invitation

If the characters decline, read or paraphrase:

"Hmm, not what I expected. Oh, well! Maybe next time." Dardew shrugs and disappears with a puff of smoke.

At your discretion, Dardew might return later to reissue his invitation, perhaps offering an important insight or piece of information in return for the characters' participation.

title: Hellfire Dome
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Hellfire Dome

Devils prize competition, treachery, and power, so they created the Hellfire Dome, a gauntlet of deadly scenarios designed to feature all three. These challenges take place in a volcanic pit on Avernus, the first layer of the Nine Hells. Just outside the arid dome lies an endless wasteland razed in the Blood War, an eternal conflict between devils and demons.

The Hellfire Dome is a multistory arena hewn from obsidian. A massive dome forged from infernal steel covers the arena, shielding it from meteors that fall from Avernus's skies. Beneath the dome, an infernal steel cage prevents contestants from escaping.

Thousands of devils gather to watch the Hellfire Games. These rowdy onlookers sometimes cast coins into the pit, showering contenders with gold. Unpopular contestants occasionally receive a ball of flame hurled by a disgruntled fiend.

Refer to the Hellfire Dome map and note that the players begin in the center of area H1. Don't reveal the rest of the map's contents yet, as it is not not initially visible to the characters.

Hellfire Dome Features

The Hellfire Dome has the following features:

  • Ambiance. The arena is dry and oppressively hot, and it reeks of blood and brimstone. The audience roars with cheers and howls.
  • Ceilings. Aside from the dome over the arena, the Hellfire Dome has no ceilings. An indestructible cage 60 feet above the pit separates contestants from the audience.
  • Lighting. Unless otherwise specified, areas in the dome are in Bright Light.
  • Portals. Each of the lettered portals on Hellfire Dome map is a gateway of harmless fire linked to another area in the arena. A creature that enters a portal emerges within 5 feet of the portal with the matching letter on Hellfire Dome map or in the nearest unoccupied space.

Dungeon Locations

The following locations are keyed to the Hellfire Dome map. The map also shows the locations of characters and monsters in the tunnels.

H1: Hellfire Arena

As the smoke clears, you find yourself in a pit within a hellish arena. The temperature is oppressively hot, and the air stinks of sulfur. Thousands of devils leer down at you from rows of seating above a twisted cage of infernal steel. Diabolical music fills the arena.

You stand on a raised platform inscribed with a pentagram. Red flames burn in five braziers, one at each of the star's points.

Dardew flies over the pit. His voice booms out, quieting the din. "Welcome, one and all, to the Hellfire Dome! Prepare yourselves for a night of death, betrayal, and vile spectacle." The audience erupts in thunderous applause.

"I present to you our latest contenders: group five hundred twenty-seven! Will they survive to become the Hellfire Club's newest initiates? Only time will tell, but we wish them luck. Let the Hellfire Games begin!"

Suddenly, five eyeless, flying demons burst from the fiery braziers.

The five Demobat fight to the death. Whenever the characters vanquish a Demobat, the audience rewards them (see "Treasure" below). Once the characters defeat the bats, five blazing portals appear along the arena's walls.

Dardew then floats down and congratulates the characters on completing their first challenge. He informs them that only after they have completed at least two more challenges can they proceed through the east portal to their final test (area H7). Dardew doesn't reveal what lies beyond any of the portals.

  • Portals. Five portals in the arena lead to the following locations:
  • Portal A. Portal A leads to area H4.
  • Portal B. Portal B leads to area H3.
  • Portal C. Portal C leads to area H7. The portal doesn't function until the characters have completed challenges in at least two other areas.
  • Portal D. Portal D leads to area H5.
  • Portal E. Portal E leads to area H2.

Each portal initially functions as a one-way door, preventing reentry until the characters have completed the challenge in the destination area.

Treasure

Each time a character kills a Demobat, the audience throws 50 GP into this area.

Dardew amuses a cultist of Demogorgon during a trivia round of Fiend Feud

H2: Fiend Feud

Dardew hovers impatiently over this room, which features two rusty, wrought-iron podiums that resemble corroded coffins. Five masked cultists stand behind one of the podiums, while the other is vacant.

"It's that time again!" Dardew announces to the devils above. "Are you ready for another game of Fiend Feud?" The audience cheers. "Contestants, take your places." Dardew clears his throat and gestures to the empty podium.

This challenge is called Fiend Feud, a trivia game of brains and bloodshed where two teams compete for fame, fortune—and their lives. The opposing team consists of five Cultist of Demogorgon who are Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters. Dardew acts as host.

Once the characters take their places behind the podium, the game begins.

  • Playing Fiend Feud. Fiend Feud is a trivia game with three rounds and a mostly arbitrary points system. The game's rules are as follows:
  • Trivia Questions. Each round, Dardew asks the characters one question from the Fiend Feud Questions table, rerolling duplicates. These questions test player knowledge as much as character knowledge. The player characters are allowed to briefly deliberate before giving their response. If they answer the question correctly, their team receives 1 point.
  • Chance to Steal. If the characters answer a question incorrectly, the opposing team has a chance answer the question, receiving 1 point if they answer it correctly. The cultists are well-versed in occult lore and answer any such questions correctly, but they know little about anything else and get those questions wrong. The cultists know the answers to questions 1, 4, and 6 in the Fiend Feud Questions table.
  • Bonus Round. After three rounds of trivia, both teams can earn bonus points by killing members of the opposing team. Have everyone roll Initiative. For each opposing team member they slay, a team earns 1 point.

The game ends when only one team remains.

If you really want to run a certain encounter, you can just have whichever portal the characters go through lead to that area. It's an old DM trick I like to call "the invisible railroad."

Fiend Feud Questions
1d6QuestionAnswer
1What vile lich is missing one eye and one hand?Vecna
2What creatures love brains but loathe zombies?Mind flayers
3Which vampire lord rules over the land of Barovia?Count Strahd von Zarovich
4Which demon lord is the self-styled Prince of Demons?Demogorgon
5Which warrior severed the hand of a famous lich?Kas
6Which archdevil rules over all the Nine Hells?Asmodeus

At the DM's discretion, a character can take the Study action to make a 15 Intelligence (Arcana or Religion) check to know the answer to a question, learning the correct answer on a successful check.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Correct Answers. Whenever a character correctly answers a question, the audience throws 10 GP into this area.
  • Slaying Cultists. Whenever a character slays a cultist, the audience throws 25 GP into this area.
  • Winning the Game. If the characters win Fiend Feud, the audience showers them with 150 GP.

H3: Demonic Incursion

This fetid chamber holds a bubbling well of brownish sludge. In front of the well, a devil stands poised for battle. Glaive in hand, the devil sports a writhing beard of barbed, snakelike appendages.

"Fight well alongside me, maggots," it spits, "Or I'll stick you like the smelly flesh bags you are!" Just then, the well burps up six squealing demons, each more hideous than the last.

An unseen creature whispers in your ear. "Kill the demons, then kill this devil—make it look like an accident, and you'll be rewarded. You have my word!"

A dretch bursts forth from a demonic well
  • DM Secret!. Don't reveal the Imp Trickster yet. This monster is invisible.

Six Dretch erupt from the well. The Hostile [Attitude] demons fight the characters and the Bearded Devil, which is initially Indifferent [Attitude] toward the party and fights alongside them. Once all six dretches have been slain, the challenge is complete, and the portal to area H1 reopens.

A treacherous Imp Trickster with the Invisible condition watches the battle unfold. The imp loathes the bearded devil and wishes it dead but is Indifferent [Attitude] toward the characters. During the battle, the imp encourages characters to turn on the bearded devil when the last dretch falls.

The Devil You Don't Know

The bearded devil is an overbearing grunt who barks orders at the characters and scolds any who defy its commands. Whenever a character slays a demon, the bearded devil loudly takes credit for the kill.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating the Bearded Devil. If a character kills the bearded devil, the imp turns visible and gives them 200 GP.
  • Defeating Dretches. Each time a character kills a dretch, the audience throws 50 GP into this area.
  • Defeating the Imp. If a character kills the Imp Trickster, the bearded devil thanks the characters for eliminating "the spy" and gives them 10 GP.

H4: Sanctuary of Yeenoghu

Three mangy, hyenoid fiends conduct a ritual in this wicked sanctuary. In the center of the chamber, a giant, wicked-looking flail spins and stops at unpredictable intervals, violently swinging its three spiked heads.

Two of the creatures cackle maliciously as the third—completely hairless—chants, "Yeenoghu! Deliver us from this wretched game so we may spill blood in your name!"

Three Gnoll Warrior beseech the demon lord Yeenoghu for aid in this sanctuary. They are Hostile [Attitude] toward all other creatures and rush them on sight.

These are the same gnolls from the Dungeon of Shadows (see "The Vanishing Gnome"). They have since died and made their way to the Hellfire Dome. If the characters fought them previously, the gnolls recognize them and greet them accordingly:

The gnolls visibly seethe with hatred. "You again?!" shouts the hairless gnoll. "Heretics! How dare you come here and interrupt our ritual a second time!"

The gnolls fight to the death (again).

Flail

The spinning flail is embedded in the ground between the gnolls. Each round on Initiative count 10 (losing Initiative ties), the flail's three heads crash to the ground. Each creature within 10 feet of the flail must succeed on a 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 3d6 Bludgeoning damage and have the Prone condition. The flail doesn't harm the gnolls.

The flail has AC 18, HP 40, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. If the flail is destroyed, it stops spinning, and the audience roars in jubilation.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating Gnolls. Each time a character kills a gnoll, the audience throws 100 GP into this area.
  • Destroying the Flail. If a character destroys the flail, the audience throws 200 GP into this area.

H5: Infernal Court

A judge with a nest of snakes for hair and wearing crimson robes presides over this infernal court. Two short podiums rest before the judge's bench, an imposing monument of black marble flanked by two snarling hounds; flames drip from the hounds' jaws. A lone imp perches atop one of the podiums. It snickers as you enter.

Nine petrified jurors with frightened expressions fill a juror's box to the north. The judge calls the court to order. "Order in the court!" the judge demands. "The accused have finally decided to join us—late and without representation. How do you plead?"

The judge is Yudith Duboix, a no-nonsense Medusa. Judge Deboix is Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters, who have just entered their own trial. Two Hell Hound ferociously obey the judge's commands.

The trial proceeds through arraignment, statements, and sentencing, as detailed in the following sections. The characters can either represent themselves or allow the Imp Trickster, an unlicensed attorney, to provide them with bad-faith representation.

The jury is composed of adventurers petrified by Judge Deboix. If the characters try to fight the court instead, they might be similarly turned to stone, in which case Dardew can amend his contract (see "Infernal Contract" earlier in this adventure) to also remove the Petrified condition.

  • Arraignment. After the characters' plea, Judge Duboix summarizes the charges against them, which might include but aren't limited to the following:
  • Arson. A character is charged with arson if they've ever set anything on fire, including torches.
  • Failure to Appear. A character is charged with failure to appear if their player has ever arrived late to a game session.
  • Murder. A character is charged with murder if they've ever slain a creature in combat.
  • Thievery. A character is charged with thievery if they've ever stolen property, including gold or items found in a dungeon or taken from the dead.
  • Trespassing. A character is charged with trespassing if they've ever entered a location, including a dungeon, without permission.

At your discretion, other offenses might be worthy of a charge in this kangaroo court.

Statements

The characters can confer and give a statement in their defense. A character can try to convince Judge Duboix of the party's innocence and make a 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check. On a successful check, Judge Duboix finds the party not guilty and dismisses the characters from the court. On a failed check (or if the characters chose to let the imp represent them), Judge Duboix rules against the party and moves to sentencing.

If the party is found not guilty, the challenge is considered complete, and the portal to area H1 reopens.

Judge Yudith Duboix, a stone-cold medusa judge, demands order in the infernal court

Sentencing

Judge Duboix's sentencing is harsh and swift. If the party is found guilty, the medusa sentences the characters to 1,000 years in prison. The judge then orders the hell hounds to escort the characters to the infernal prison (area H6) for detainment. If the characters refuse, the hell hounds leap into battle. Judge Duboix defends itself as necessary but otherwise abstains from combat. If both hounds are slain, Judge Duboix surrenders and overturns the previous verdict.

If the characters comply with sentencing and later return to this area, the courtroom is empty, and the portal to area H1 reopens.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating Hell Hounds. Each time a character kills a hound, the audience throws 200 GP into this area.
  • Defeating Judge Duboix. If Judge Duboix dies, the audience throws 2,000 GP into this area.
  • Innocent Verdict. If the party is found innocent, the audience throws 100 GP into this area.

H6: Infernal Prison

A devil covered in sharp barbs patrols this open-air cell block. The devil rattles its tail against the bars of the six cages, laughing cruelly at the prisoners. A key hangs around the devil's neck.

The warden of this prison is a masochistic Barbed Devil named Khaos, the Bringer of Pain. Khaos is Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters. When they enter, the devil grunts and points them to the biggest cage (cage 1), attacking any who refuse to enter. Khaos then returns to marching up and down the block.

Khaos enjoys catching escaped prisoners and breaking their spirits and bodies. The devil doesn't confiscate inmates' equipment and pretends not to notice if they try to free themselves or one another. Khaos doesn't pursue runaways beyond this area.

Cages

Khaos wears the key to these six locked cages. As a Utilize action, a character can try to pick a cage's lock using Thieves' Tools, doing so with a successful 15 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. The check is made with Disadvantage if the character is trying to pick the lock from inside the cage.

Alternatively, a character can try to goad Khaos into unlocking their cage. As an Influence action, a character can taunt the barbed devil and make a 13 Charisma (Performance) check. On a successful check, Khaos unlocks the door, enters the cage, and strikes that character to teach them a lesson.

The cage's contents are as follows:

  • Cage 1 contains only a bench chained to the wall.
  • Cage 2 contains a Demogorgon Spawn captured on the battlefields of Avernus. The spawn is Hostile [Attitude] toward all other creatures and tries to tear them limb from limb if freed from its cell.
  • Cage 3 is empty.
  • Cage 4 contains a human Cultist of Demogorgon who warns any who address her that the "Sibilant Beast" will consume them all. The Hostile [Attitude] cultist fights any who enter her cell.
  • Cage 5 contains an Imp Trickster playing a harmonica. The imp is Indifferent [Attitude] toward the characters but aids them in combat in this area if freed.
  • Cage 6 is empty.

If a character escapes their cage or frees one of the other imprisoned creatures, Khaos brays with malevolent laughter and fights the escapee.

Treasure

Characters receive treasure as follows:

  • Defeating Khaos. If a character kills Khaos, the audience throws 2,000 GP into this area.
  • Defeating the Demogorgon Spawn. If a character kills the Demogorgon Spawn, the audience throws 150 GP into this area.

H7: Demodragon Lair

Dardew has tilted the odds in the characters' favor. When they enter this area, each character magically gains the benefits of finishing a Short Rest. Then, read or paraphrase the following text:

A river of molten lava flows through this scorched lair. Crumbling rubble, dried viscera, and cracked bones litter the ground, a barren landscape marred by past battles.

The earth trembles as a massive abomination with a sickly gray hide, razor-sharp claws, and two faceless heads rises from a mound of glittering treasure. It stretches its wide, leathery wings and unfurls its heads to reveal two gaping maws of toothed, fleshy petals. The behemoth bellows two bone-chilling roars.

Roll initiative!

The final challenge in the Hellfire Games is the Demodragon, an abomination that has slaughtered scores of contestants. The Demodragon is Hostile [Attitude] toward the characters and fights to the death.

  • Lava. Rivers of lava flow throughout this area, as shown on the map. A creature that enters the lava for the first time on a turn or starts its turn in the lava takes 6d10 fire damage.

Treasure

The Demodragon's hoard contains the following: an Adamantine Breastplate, a Spiked Shield, a Potion of Healing, and 2,420 GP.

The Demodragon rouses from its slumber to devour foolhardy contestants

title: Conclusion
folder: Stranger Things: Welcome to the Hellfire Club
html:
Conclusion

The Hellfire Games conclude when the characters vanquish the Demodragon or die trying. If the characters defeat the Demodragon, read or paraphrase the following text:

With an earthshaking crash, the Demodragon collapses dead before you. The crowd goes wild.

Dardew soars overhead. "Wow! What a show!" he crows. "Friends and fiends, please join me in welcoming our latest Hellfire champions!"

He flies toward you and says quietly, "Adventurers, now would be a great time to take a bow. You've earned it."

In addition to the treasure they collected in the Hellfire Dome, the characters earn the following rewards for winning the Hellfire Games:

  • Hellfire Club Membership. Dardew invites characters to join the Hellfire Club. If they accept his invitation, they each receive a pendant worth 50 GP. The pendant depicts the face of a red devil flanked by a flail and flaming sword.
  • Hellfire Hall of Fame. The characters are inducted into the Hellfire Hall of Fame. Their names are recorded forever in the annals of infernal history alongside other legendary heroes and villains.
  • Voiding the Infernal Contract. If any character entered into an infernal contract with Dardew (see "Infernal Contract" earlier in this adventure), Dardew voids the contract.

When the characters are ready to leave the Nine Hells, Dardew magically returns them to Greyhawkins. Before he departs, Dardew thanks them for the magnificent performance.

Congratulations.

Hellfire is officially in your hands.

You should take a bow, too. Being a DM can feel overwhelming sometimes, but know this: You're not alone. I promise. If you ever need a pep talk, I'm just a phone call away. Save me a seat at your table. I'll be back to see what you've done with the place.

You should take a bow, too. Being a DM can feel overwhelming sometimes, but know this: You're not alone. I promise. If you ever need a pep talk, I'm just a phone call away. Save me a seat at your table. I'll be back to see what you've done with the place.

Appendix D - Pre-Generated Characters

Dungeons & Dragons is a cooperative game in which players create exciting fantasy stories guided by a Dungeon Master, or DM.

Imagination and chance determine the fate of the players' characters.

Playing a Character

Choose a character. Team up. Venture forth.

Being the Dungeon Master

Run the Adventure. Guide the story. Adjudicate the rules.

A Note From Eddie

Allow me to let you in on a little secret: nobody knows all the rules by heart. I sure as hell don't. That's what these guides are for. The rules are there to help everyone at the table tell a story. If you ever feel like the rules are getting in the way of that, remember the most important rule of all: have fun.

At the end of the day, that's all that matters.

Sundar the Bold

Human Fighter

A gallant and unyielding warrior, Sundar the Bold bravely defends his companions—just like this Fighter's player, Lucas Sinclair.

D&D Beyond Character

    • Level 1
    • Level 2
    • Level 3
    • Level 2: Automatically gain Action Surge
    • Level 3: Choose the Champion subclass

Will the Wise

Human Wizard

Will Byer's Wizard is a mainstay of the party and is always up for another adventure. When Will the Wise casts a spell, his magic sometimes manifests in unexpected colors.

D&D Beyond Character

    • Level 1
    • Level 2
    • Level 3
    • Level 2: Choose a Skill for Expertise
    • Level 3: Choose the Evoker subclass

Lady Applejack

Elf Rogue

Played by Erica Sinclair, Lady Applejack is a Chaotic Good, Elf Rogue who will sneak behind any monster, stab them in the back with her kukri, and smile as she watches them die a slow, agonizing death.

D&D Beyond Character

    • Level 1
    • Level 2
    • Level 3
    • Level 2: Automatically gain Cunning Action
    • Level 3: Choose the Assassin subclass

Nog the Dwarf

Dwarf Cleric

Dustin Henderson's sturdy Cleric, Nog, has gotten his companions out of a bind more times than he can count. Nog is a devotee of Heironeous, a god of chivalry, justice, and war.

D&D Beyond Character

    • Level 1
    • Level 2
    • Level 3
    • Level 2: Automatically gain Channel Divinity
    • Level 3: Choose the War Domain subclass

Tayr the Paladin

Halfling Paladin

When Mike Wheeler isn't behind the DM screen in his parents' basement, he dusts off his trusty Paladin Tayr. The heart of the party, Tayr unites his companions and leads the charge in their fight against evil.

D&D Beyond Character

    • Level 1
    • Level 2
    • Level 3
    • Level 2: Automatically gain Divine Smite
    • Level 3: Choose the Oath of Devotion subclass
